suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The Google Meet fallback dereferences mainHostDestinationCalendar without checking whether the destination array is empty. Bookings with Google Meet and no configured destination now throw instead of falling back to Cal Video. Use mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration in the condition.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The reference mapping discards credentialId for every video result. createMeeting returns the video credential ID, and handleCancelBooking only deletes a video meeting when its reference has that ID, so newly created video meetings are left behind on cancellation. Preserve result.credentialId for video results as well.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Office365 creation always selects the first host's destination despite being invoked separately with each host's credential. A collective booking with distinct Office365 calendars sends the second host's token to the first host's calendar ID, causing failed or incorrectly targeted creation. Accept the credentialId supplied by CalendarManager and select the matching destination.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The fallback searches for a destination whose externalId equals the absent externalCalendarId. When a booking reference lacks that field, this yields undefined instead of the configured calendar and the update request has no calendarId; the analogous deletion fallback targets primary rather than the configured calendar. Restore a valid destination fallback when the reference has no externalCalendarId.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The optional push discards all collected team destinations when the organizer has no destination calendar. A collective booking with configured secondary hosts therefore creates none of their calendar events even though teamDestinationCalendars contains them. Initialize the array before appending the team destinations.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: updateLocation now reads externalId and credentialId exclusively from results, but CalendarManager.updateEvent returns neither field. Calendar references produced by location editing consequently lose their calendar and credential routing information, breaking subsequent updates or cancellation, particularly for secondary collective hosts. Return those fields from updateEvent or preserve them from the corresponding booking reference.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The new per-reference loop runs the recurring-series deletion branch for every host, but that branch still iterates only bookingToDelete.user.credentials and selects the first calendar reference in each occurrence. Canceling all remaining collective occurrences repeatedly deletes the owner's events while leaving secondary hosts' events untouched. For each occurrence, delete the reference matching the current host credential using the resolved calendarCredential.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Organization creation no longer assigns a slug when team billing is disabled, while requestedSlug is also omitted in that mode. New self-hosted organizations therefore have neither publication field, and publish.handler rejects them because requestedSlug is missing. Restore the non-billing slug assignment.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Select the destination belonging to the current credential rather than always taking the first array entry. EventManager now calls createEvent once per destination with that destination's credential, while passing the full event array each time. In a collective booking with two Outlook hosts, the second host therefore attempts to insert into the first host's calendar using the second host's token, typically failing instead of creating the second calendar event. Accept the credentialId passed by CalendarManager and match the destination by that ID (or pass a destination-specific event).

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Preserve the optional guard when checking the first destination (`mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration`). When Google Meet is selected and destinationCalendar is null or empty (both explicitly produced by booking handlers), destructuring yields undefined and this condition throws instead of falling back to Cal Video.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Select the destination belonging to the credential passed by CalendarManager, rather than always selecting the first array element. EventManager now invokes creation for each collective host with the full destination array. A second Office365 host therefore attempts to write to the first host's calendar using its own token, causing creation to fail or target the wrong calendar; meanwhile the saved reference records the second host's externalId.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Initialize destinationCalendar to an array before appending collective hosts' destinations. When neither the event type nor organizer has a destination, it is set to null above, so optional push silently discards all the computed teamDestinationCalendars. Hosts with configured destination calendars consequently receive no calendar events.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Retain result.credentialId for non-calendar references as well. The previous mapping saved the dedicated video integration's credential ID; this change unconditionally replaces it with undefined for video results, losing the association needed to identify the account that created the meeting during subsequent lifecycle operations.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Preserve the missing-destination fallback by using mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration here. handleNewBooking explicitly supplies null when neither the event type nor organizer has a destination calendar, and other callers supply []. With a Google Meet location, destructuring yields undefined and this property access throws instead of falling back to Cal Video as the previous optional access did.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Select the destination matching the credentialId passed by CalendarManager rather than always taking the first destination. EventManager now invokes createEvent once per collective host using that host's credential but passes the entire destination array each time. For two Office365 hosts, the second host therefore attempts to create an event in the first host's calendar under /me/calendars, normally failing because that calendar does not belong to the second account. Accept the credentialId argument and resolve the corresponding destination, as the Google implementation does.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Select the destination matching the credential used for this creation rather than always taking the first element. handleNewBooking now appends collective hosts' calendars, and EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents calls CalendarManager.createEvent separately for each host's credential with the entire event array. On the second Office365 host, this code therefore requests the organizer's calendar ID using the second host's token, typically failing with a calendar-not-found error instead of creating the event on that host's calendar. Accept the credentialId passed by CalendarManager and use it to select the appropriate destination.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Keep the first destination access optional in the Google Meet fallback. The changed handleNewBooking producer explicitly sets destinationCalendar to null when neither the event type nor organizer has a destination, and other changed callers produce an empty array. Destructuring either yields no first destination, so selecting Google Meet now throws at mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration instead of falling back to Cal Video as before. Use mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Guard mainHostDestinationCalendar before reading integration. When destinationCalendar is null or [], destructuring produces undefined; a booking with MeetLocationType then throws a TypeError instead of falling back to Cal Video. handleNewBooking explicitly still produces null when neither the event type nor organizer has a destination, so this is reachable in precisely the no-calendar case this fallback handles.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Select the destination belonging to the credential used for this creation, rather than always taking the first destination. createAllCalendarEvents now invokes this service for each collective host's credential but passes the full destination array each time. The second Office365 host consequently posts to the first host's calendar ID under the second host's token, normally failing because that calendar is inaccessible; if accessible, it writes to the wrong calendar while the booking reference records the second host's destination.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: For cancel-all-remaining recurring collective bookings, delete each updated booking's reference matching the current outer reference/credential. The new outer loop iterates all calendar references, but this inner block still iterates only the organizer's credentials and takes the first calendar reference of each booking. Every outer iteration therefore repeats deletion of the first host's event, while the additional hosts' recurring events remain on their calendars after cancellation.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The admin-or-owner authorization check requires both isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner to succeed. Since isTeamAdmin accepts ADMIN and OWNER but isTeamOwner accepts only OWNER, a team admin who is not the organizer or an attendee receives FORBIDDEN. Use isTeamAdmin alone, or combine the checks with OR.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: uniqueGuests filters against existing attendees but does not deduplicate addresses within the incoming guests array. A direct mutation with the same new address twice inserts two Attendee records and sends duplicate invitations because the server schema permits duplicates and the Attendee model has no unique booking/email constraint. Deduplicate normalized input before filtering and inserting.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: The blacklist comparison uses the raw guest address against lowercase blacklist entries instead of the canonical address used by handleNewBooking. An authorized attendee can invite a blocked address using uppercase characters or a plus-address alias, bypassing the guest-email block and triggering an invitation. Compare extractBaseEmail(guest).toLowerCase() against normalized blacklist entries, as the existing booking flow does.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: EventManager is initialized with the requesting user's credentials rather than the booking organizer's credentials. When an attendee or team owner adds guests to a booking whose calendar reference lacks credentialId, updateAllCalendarEvents selects credentials by type from the caller's calendars, so the organizer's event is not updated or the update targets the wrong account. Load credentials for booking.userId and initialize the manager with the booking owner.

suggestions.label: performance
suggestions.suggestionContent: The mutation accepts an unbounded guest array that is persisted and immediately expanded into concurrent emails to every attendee. For non-seated bookings each email's ICS serializes the full attendee list, so adding N guests creates O(N) concurrent sends and O(N²) aggregate attachment work; repeated additions also resend to all existing attendees. Enforce a server-side guest-count and total-attendee limit before insertion and bound notification concurrency.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: The blacklist entries are lowercased at line 71, but `guest` is not normalized before `includes`. Both the UI and server schemas accept mixed-case emails without lowercasing, so a caller can submit `Blocked@Example.com` to bypass a configured `blocked@example.com` blacklist and have that address added and emailed. Normalize the incoming address to the same lowercase representation before checking the blacklist (preferably normalize guest inputs once before identity comparisons).

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The new removal tooltip hard-codes `Remove email`, so users in non-English locales see English text even though the neighbouring controls use `t(...)` and this component already obtains `t` from useLocale. Route this tooltip through a translation key (and supply its English translation) rather than using the literal.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Enforce guest uniqueness on the server, including atomically against existing attendees. This filter checks each submitted address only against the original booking snapshot, so a request with guests ["new@example.com", "new@example.com"] retains both and passes both entries to createMany, despite the dialog's explicit uniqueness requirement. Two concurrent requests for the same new address can likewise both pass this check before insertion. Deduplicate/validate the input and enforce booking/email uniqueness transactionally or with a database constraint so duplicate requests cannot create duplicate attendees (or surface a database constraint error after validation).

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Pass `uniqueGuests` rather than `guests` to `sendAddGuestsEmails`. The new email-manager implementation interprets this argument as the attendees newly added and sends `AttendeeScheduledEmail` to every attendee whose email it contains. If the request contains an existing attendee and a new guest, the existing attendee is filtered out of the database insertion but remains in `guests`, so they receive a new-booking notification rather than `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail`. Using the filtered insertion list preserves the email manager's distinction between existing and new attendees.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: uniqueGuests does not deduplicate the submitted guests: it only filters against attendees already in the booking. The server schema accepts duplicates, so submitting ["new@example.com", "new@example.com"] passes this filter and creates two attendee records (and sends duplicate invitations). Deduplicate the input on the server before creating attendees rather than relying on the dialog's uniqueness check.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Blacklist entries are lowercased at lines 70–72, but guest input is compared without lowercasing. An address such as Blocked@example.com therefore bypasses a blacklist entry blocked@example.com and is added and emailed. Normalize both sides of the comparison consistently.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Pass uniqueGuests rather than guests to sendAddGuestsEmails. If the submitted list contains an existing attendee plus a new address, the existing attendee is filtered out of creation but remains in guests. The email manager uses this argument to classify new attendees, so that existing attendee receives a fresh scheduled invitation instead of the guests-added notification.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The sync branch returns a native fetch Response even for callers whose original refresh function returns a parsed token object or an Axios/Gaxios response. Google reads res.data.access_token, Zoho CRM/Bigin read response.data.error, and HubSpot reads accessToken/expiresIn directly, so enabling synchronization breaks those refresh paths regardless of the endpoint's JSON payload. Normalize the endpoint response to each caller's expected contract, or make all callers consume a common parsed-token contract.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The computed object keys stringify Zod schema objects rather than matching arbitrary token fields. Zod object parsing strips undeclared fields, so expires_in, expiry_date and actual refresh_token fields are discarded in synchronization mode; Zoom then computes expiry_date from undefined and Google loses required credential fields. Declare the supported expiry fields explicitly and preserve additional response fields with passthrough or catchall.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The parser fabricates the literal refresh token "refresh_token" whenever a successful response omits refresh_token, including when synchronization is disabled. Office365's response schema explicitly permits that omission, and its caller merges parsed data over existing credentials, replacing the valid saved refresh token with this invalid value and breaking the next refresh. Leave the property absent so the existing token survives the merge.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Google persists the entire safeParse result returned by parseRefreshTokenResponse instead of its data property. Even with credential sharing disabled, the stored key becomes {success:true,data:{...}} rather than the credential object, so the next service construction fails googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key). Persist the successful result's data property.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Bigin passes credentialId as the userId argument to refreshOAuthTokens. This value originates from credential.id, so synchronization sends the credential primary key as calcomUserId and requests tokens for the wrong user; team credentials also incorrectly enter the user-sync branch. Thread credential.userId through refreshAccessToken and pass that value instead.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The new credential update references prisma without importing or declaring it; searching this file finds only the new usage. This fails TypeScript checking and raises ReferenceError after a successful token exchange at runtime. Import prisma from @calcom/prisma before using it.

suggestions.label: performance
suggestions.suggestionContent: getClient now unconditionally exchanges the Salesforce refresh token on every service construction, even when the saved access token is valid. Each constructor invocation adds a blocking OAuth network round trip and credential database write before any Salesforce operation, replacing jsforce's existing on-demand refresh behavior. Keep refresh on demand or guard the exchange with a token-expiration check.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The webhook performs a non-atomic findFirst followed by create when no credential exists. Concurrent deliveries for the same user and app can both observe no row and insert duplicates because Credential has no unique userId/appId constraint; subsequent findFirst updates only one duplicate, leaving competing credentials stale. Serialize the lookup/create operation for each user/app pair or introduce an appropriate uniqueness constraint and atomic upsert.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: The webhook authenticates a secret using direct string inequality, which is not constant-time and can leak information about the secret through comparison timing. Compare fixed-length representations using a constant-time primitive (such as crypto.timingSafeEqual), handling absent or malformed headers safely, instead of comparing the secret strings directly.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: When a refresh response omits refresh_token, this helper manufactures the hardcoded credential "refresh_token". Callers such as Office365 merge this into stored credentials, overwriting the valid existing refresh token and causing subsequent provider refreshes to use a predictable invalid token. Leave the field absent and preserve the existing credential when omission is allowed by the provider, or reject the response when a refresh token is required; do not substitute a literal authentication token.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The comment says the schema assumes any numeric property is the expiry and allows other token-response properties, but these computed keys are just the string representations of Zod schema objects, not dynamic property matchers. A normal `expires_in` or `expiry_date` field is therefore not recognized by these entries, and `z.object` does not preserve arbitrary extra properties by default. Make the documented contract match the schema (or implement explicit expiry fields and passthrough validation); otherwise integrators following this comment will supply responses that do not behave as advertised.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the Zod safeParse result ({ success: true, data: ... }), not the parsed credential object returned by the previous schema.parse call. Persist key.data instead of key here. Otherwise even with credential sharing disabled, every successful Google refresh replaces the stored credential with an envelope lacking top-level access_token, refresh_token and expiry_date, breaking subsequent credential parsing.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The sync branch returns a native fetch Response, but the changed Google caller reads res.data, the Zoho callers read tokenInfo.data, and HubSpot expects a decoded HubspotToken. Native Responses satisfy none of those contracts, so enabling sync makes these refresh paths fail or consume undefined token fields. Decode and adapt the sync response to each caller's required shape (or normalize the helper contract and update all callers); preserve Response handling for the existing fetch-based consumers.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The third parameter of refreshOAuthTokens is a user ID and is serialized as calcomUserId, but this call passes credentialId. These IDs are unrelated, so the sync endpoint refreshes the wrong user's credentials or cannot find the user; team credentials also incorrectly enter the user-sync branch. Pass the credential owner's userId (null for team credentials), rather than the credential primary key.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Persist the parsed credential data, not the safeParse result. Previously googleCredentialSchema.parse returned the credential object directly; parseRefreshTokenResponse returns { success: true, data: ... }. Passing that wrapper as key stores access_token, expiry_date and refresh_token under data rather than at the credential root, so subsequent Google credential parsing fails even with credential sharing disabled. Use the helper result's data.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Normalize the sync response to the consuming provider's expected shape. This branch returns a native fetch Response, whereas Google reads res.data.access_token, Zoho CRM/Bigin read tokenInfo.data.error, and HubSpot expects a decoded HubspotToken. None of those consumers decode the sync Response, so enabling sync breaks their refresh paths despite a successful endpoint response. Decode and adapt the response or update each of these consumers to handle the native Response explicitly.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Pass the credential owner's userId rather than credentialId. The new refreshOAuthTokens contract uses its third argument as calcomUserId in the sync request (and to distinguish user credentials). Credential IDs are unrelated to user IDs, so sync requests target the wrong user whenever those IDs differ, potentially refreshing another user's credentials or failing to find the intended account.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the safeParse result ({ success, data }), not the parsed credential object. Persisting this as key replaces the Google credential's top-level access_token, refresh_token and expiry_date with an envelope, breaking subsequent credential parsing even when sharing is disabled. Persist the successful result's data instead.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The sync branch returns a native fetch Response, but Google reads res.data, Zoho CRM/Bigin read response.data, and HubSpot expects an already-decoded HubspotToken. Consequently these integrations fail or receive undefined tokens whenever sync is enabled. Decode and adapt the sync response to each caller's expected representation (or standardize both branches and consumers).

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Computed keys using z.string().toString() do not validate arbitrary response properties: they produce literal object keys (normally '[object Object]'), and the second declaration overwrites the first. Zod object parsing strips unrecognized fields, so ordinary expires_in/expiry_date and refresh_token fields are discarded on the sharing path. Define explicit expiry fields or a schema that preserves and validates the actual response properties; otherwise consumers cannot calculate token expiry.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The helper's third argument is a userId and is sent as calcomUserId, but credentialId here is credential.id (confirmed at its assignment and refreshAccessToken parameter). When these IDs differ, the sync endpoint requests tokens for the wrong user or cannot find the user. Pass the owning credential.userId separately rather than the credential primary key.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the safeParse result ({ success: true, data: ... }), not the parsed credentials. Persisting this value as `key` on the next lines replaces the credential with that wrapper even with sharing disabled. Subsequent readers expecting top-level access_token/refresh_token cannot use it. Persist the parsed result's data instead.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Computed property names using Zod schemas do not define wildcard fields: both schemas stringify to an object string key. Zod objects also strip unrecognized fields by default. Consequently a normal sync response containing access_token and expiry_date/expires_in parses with its expiry stripped (as well as other token fields). Office365 and Zoom then merge/persist credentials without the new expiry, while Google loses even more credential fields. Define explicit supported expiry fields and preserve/validate additional token properties rather than using schema objects as property names.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The sync branch returns a raw fetch Response, whereas the Google, HubSpot and Zoho callbacks supplied to this helper return SDK token objects or Axios/Gaxios responses. With sharing enabled, Google reads `res.data` and then `token.access_token`, and Zoho reads `tokenInfo.data.error`, causing undefined-property exceptions; HubSpot similarly consumes token fields directly. Normalize the sync response to each caller's expected representation (or normalize both branches and update consumers) before returning it.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The new database update inside catch can itself throw when a reminder has been deleted during scheduling. Booking cancellation deletes reminders through handleCancelBooking and deleteScheduledSMSReminder, so a concurrent cancellation followed by a scheduling error now rejects the entire cron handler and prevents the remaining reminders from being processed. Use an updateMany filtered by the reminder ID to tolerate an already-deleted row, and guard errors from retry bookkeeping so they do not escape the per-reminder error handler.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Retry counts are assigned from the stale findMany snapshot instead of incremented atomically, both here and in the catch branch. Two overlapping cron requests can each fail scheduling the same reminder with retryCount zero and both write one, so two failed attempts do not reach the deletion threshold and additional attempts are scheduled. Use Prisma's atomic retryCount increment operation in both failure branches.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Keep retry bookkeeping best-effort inside this error handler. Previously a scheduling error was logged and the loop continued; now, if workflowReminder.update rejects (for example because the reminder was concurrently deleted, or the database failure that caused the original error persists), that rejection escapes the catch and aborts the handler, leaving all subsequent reminders unprocessed. Protect this update with its own error handling so recording a failed attempt cannot break the scheduler's continue-on-error contract.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Update the cleanup comment to describe the new retry-exhaustion deletion branch. It currently says this deletes scheduled SMS reminders whose date has passed, but this OR branch also deletes any reminder with retryCount > 1, including future-dated reminders and without an SMS restriction. The comment now misrepresents the scope of this destructive operation.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Restrict retry-limit deletion to unscheduled SMS reminders (or reset retryCount when scheduling succeeds). A reminder can fail twice, enter the next invocation with retryCount = 2, and successfully schedule; the success update does not reset that count. This unconditional OR arm deletes that successfully scheduled future reminder on the following run, losing its tracking/reference before delivery. It also removes the SMS method restriction from this cleanup arm.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The failure counter uses a stale read-modify-write value. If two cron executions select the same reminder at retryCount 0 and both fail, each writes 1, losing one failure; the reminder survives the > 1 cleanup threshold and can receive extra retries. Use Prisma's atomic `retryCount: { increment: 1 }` in both this update and the catch-path update so concurrent failures are not overwritten.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: The backup-code branch accepts a valid backup code even when an arbitrary nonempty totpCode has skipped password verification. The preceding guards at lines 113–125 trust the presence of totpCode, but this new branch does not validate it, allowing a holder of a backup code to log in to a password account without knowing its password by submitting both fields. Require password verification for backup-code authentication rather than allowing an unverified totpCode to bypass it.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: Backup-code consumption overwrites the encrypted list by user ID without checking that the stored list still matches the value read before verification. Concurrent requests can both authenticate with the same single-use code, and requests using different codes can overwrite each other's removals and restore a consumed code. Use a conditional atomic update matching the original backupCodes ciphertext and reject or retry authentication if no row was updated.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Successful enablement no longer invokes onEnable until the backup-code screen's explicit Close button is clicked. Dismissing that screen through the dialog's onOpenChange instead only closes it in the parent and does not invalidate viewer.me, leaving the settings switch showing disabled even though the server has enabled 2FA. Ensure dismissal after successful enablement also invokes the completion callback and resets the setup state.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The handler shows “Backup codes copied!” immediately after calling `navigator.clipboard.writeText`, without awaiting its promise. If clipboard access is denied or the write otherwise rejects, the user still receives a success message and may close the dialog believing their recovery codes were saved. Await the clipboard write and show the success toast only after it resolves; handle rejection with an appropriate translated failure message.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Consume backup codes atomically rather than unconditionally replacing the array read earlier. Two simultaneous login requests can read the same backupCodes value, both find the same code, and both successfully update and authenticate, violating the single-use guarantee. With different codes, the last writer also restores the code consumed by the first writer. Use a conditional update against the original encrypted value and require exactly one affected row (retry validation on contention), or serialize consumption in a transaction with an appropriate row lock.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: Backup codes are authentication secrets, but indexOf compares their plaintext strings using ordinary equality and stops at the first match. This is not a constant-time credential check and can expose comparison-dependent timing. Validate the normalized code's format/length, compare fixed-length buffers with crypto.timingSafeEqual, and scan all stored slots without early termination (including handling consumed null slots) before deciding whether authentication succeeds.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: The new backup-code verification uses indexOf on plaintext secrets, so both string comparison and array traversal are non-constant-time. This exposes a timing-dependent credential check on the endpoint that disables 2FA. Use a shared constant-time verifier that validates input length, compares fixed-length buffers with crypto.timingSafeEqual, and traverses every slot without stopping on a match.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Backup-code consumption is a non-atomic read/modify/write, so the same code can grant access more than once despite the exactly-once behavior promised by this change. Two concurrent login requests can both read the original backupCodes, pass indexOf, and successfully execute this unconditional update by user ID. Concurrent use of different codes can also overwrite each other's removal, restoring a consumed code. Consume the code atomically (for example, compare-and-swap against the original encrypted backupCodes value and require exactly one affected row before authenticating, with appropriate retry handling).

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The copy test only waits for a success toast, but the implementation emits that toast unconditionally without awaiting navigator.clipboard.writeText. Removing the clipboard write entirely, copying an empty string, or rejecting the write would still pass this test. Read the clipboard after the click and compare its contents with the displayed backup codes so the test verifies the actual copy effect.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The download assertion checks only the static filename from the anchor's download attribute. It still passes if the blob contains empty or incorrect backup codes, leaving the essential recovery-code export behavior unverified. Read the downloaded file and compare its contents to the displayed codes, including their formatting.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The header conditional ends with `end if`, leaving a modifier `if` without a condition in the generated Ruby template. Rendering any existing embedded topic fails with a template syntax error instead of displaying comments. Replace this tag with `<%- end %>`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The feed importer unconditionally reads `i.content.scrub`, although RSS entries commonly provide `description` or `content:encoded` instead of Atom `content`. Such an entry raises an exception and aborts the entire poll, including imports of subsequent entries. Select the available content field with fallbacks and handle entries with no body before calling scrub.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: Feed-provided HTML is persisted with raw_html cooking after only Nokogiri parsing and URL rewriting, which do not sanitize scripts or event-handler attributes. A malicious feed entry containing executable HTML is stored as post.cooked and executed under the forum origin when rendered, including through the new raw cooked embed view. Sanitize imported HTML with an explicit safe tag, attribute and URL-scheme allowlist before storing it or returning it from the raw_html cooking path.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The URL rewrite treats protocol-relative URLs such as `//cdn.example.com/image.jpg` as paths on the article host, producing `http://article-host/cdn.example.com/image.jpg`. Imported images and links using protocol-relative external URLs therefore point to the wrong server. Resolve both href and src using URI joining against the article URL, which also handles ordinary relative paths correctly.

suggestions.label: performance
suggestions.suggestionContent: Every uncached article retrieval synchronously downloads and processes the complete configured feed before fetching the article. Because the retrieval throttle is keyed by individual embed URL, simultaneous requests for different articles each repeat the feed download and all per-item database lookups/imports, multiplying worker load by the number of requests times feed size. Coalesce feed polling with a feed-wide throttle or lock and reuse its recent results instead of executing a full poll per article.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: Sanitize imported HTML before assigning the raw_html cook method. PollFeed passes feed content directly to import, and absolutize_urls only parses HTML and rewrites URLs; it does not remove scripts, event handlers, or dangerous link schemes. Post.cook now returns this raw content unchanged, so external feed markup becomes executable HTML when cooked content is rendered. Preserve the normal sanitization boundary even when skipping Markdown rendering.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Use a localized date formatter rather than strftime("%e %b %Y"). %b produces English month abbreviations and the fixed day-month-year order ignores the selected locale, although the neighbouring header and footer labels are translated. Embedded comments therefore show English-formatted dates for users of other locales.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: Compare e.origin to the parsed origin of discourseUrl using exact equality, not indexOf. For example, discourseUrl = 'https://forum.example.com/' accepts messages from 'https://forum.example', an unrelated origin, because that origin is a substring of the configured URL. A window on that origin with a reference to the embedding window can consequently send forged discourse-resize messages and control the iframe height. Also verify e.source === iframe.contentWindow to bind accepted messages to the intended frame.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Preserve the Disqus thread creation timestamp when switching to TopicEmbed.import_remote. The previous PostCreator call passed `created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at])`, but this replacement passes only the title, and TopicEmbed.import_remote/import never forward a timestamp to PostCreator. Imported historical topics now get the migration time as their initial post creation date while their replies retain historical dates, losing the importer's chronological fidelity. Extend the import options to forward created_at and pass the thread timestamp here.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Update this test to expect Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, user_id: nil, embed_url: embed_url), rather than synchronous TopicRetriever construction and retrieval. EmbedController#best now only enqueues the job; those calls occur in Jobs::RetrieveTopic#execute. Consequently these mock expectations are unsatisfied during the controller request under normal asynchronous execution, causing the new controller spec to fail. Test retriever construction separately at the job boundary.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Replace `end if` with `end`. The generated ERB Ruby contains an incomplete modifier conditional (`end if` with no condition), so compiling this template raises SyntaxError. Every embed request that finds an existing topic therefore fails instead of rendering the discussion.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Handle entries without `content`, including ordinary RSS entries that provide only `description`. Calling `i.content.scrub` on such an entry raises NoMethodError and aborts the entire polling run, preventing this and subsequent entries from importing. Select the appropriate available content field and handle entries with no body explicitly.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Make creation idempotent under concurrent imports. Two workers can both read no embed at line 15 and create posts before attempting the same unique embed_url insert. The unique index correctly rolls back the losing transaction, but its unhandled uniqueness exception aborts that job (and potentially the rest of a feed polling run). This is reachable when scheduled polling overlaps retrieval-triggered polling; the per-URL retrieval throttle does not serialize those paths. Handle the conflict outside the transaction and return the winning embed/post, or serialize imports for the URL.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Resolve relative href/src references with URI joining rather than handling only leading slashes. For an article at http://example.com/blog/article, href='next' and src='images/photo.jpg' remain relative and resolve against the forum instead of the imported article. Moreover, '//cdn.example.com/photo.jpg' is rewritten to 'http://example.com/cdn.example.com/photo.jpg'. Both yield incorrect links/images in imported posts; apply proper URI resolution to both anchors and images.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: This test expects TopicRetriever.new and retrieve during the controller request, but EmbedController#best now only enqueues :retrieve_topic. Those synchronous expectations are not satisfied by the new implementation. Assert Jobs.enqueue with the expected embed_url/user_id here and test retriever invocation in the job test instead.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The missing-embed_url test does not establish a valid embeddable host and referer, so ensure_embeddable rejects this request before best reaches params.require(:embed_url). It also only checks non-success despite claiming a 404. Removing the required-parameter check would therefore leave this test green. Configure an allowed host/referer for this case and assert the intended missing-parameter response.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The URL and username prerequisite tests never enable feed polling (whose configured default is false) or supply the other required setting. execute consequently short-circuits at feed_polling_enabled? and never evaluates the prerequisite each test claims to cover. Both tests still pass if their corresponding presence checks are removed. Set all other prerequisites to valid values before making only the setting under test absent, so the poll_feed.never expectation actually detects removal of that guard.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The migration indexes the first category-query result before checking whether any row was returned. An installation without a persisted embed_category setting, or with no matching category name, aborts migration before reaching the uncategorized fallback. Check whether the result contains a row before accessing its id and handle missing fallback settings as well.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Legacy hosts are inserted verbatim instead of applying the new model's scheme/path normalization. Existing values such as http://discourse.org or https://example.com/1234 remain in the table, while record_for_host compares only URI.host, so previously configured embedding hosts stop working after upgrade. Normalize migrated entries to the same representation used by the model before inserting them.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Host lookup compares URI.host against a stored value that validation explicitly permits to include a port. Saving example.com:8080 succeeds, but a request from http://example.com:8080 produces URI.host equal to example.com and never matches that record, disabling embedding and retrieval for the configured host. Use a consistent port representation in both storage and lookup.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The save callback overwrites the category using categoryId even when the server substituted the uncategorized category for a blank selection. Adding a host without choosing a category therefore leaves its category badge empty, and editing it reads an undefined category id despite a valid category_id having been returned. Resolve the category from the saved response's category_id rather than the submitted selection.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Update passes the nullable result of where(...).first directly to save_host, which immediately assigns host.host. Updating a nonexistent or concurrently deleted record returns an internal error instead of a not-found response; destroy has the same lookup failure. Use find or explicitly raise a not-found error before dereferencing the lookup result.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: Normalize the parsed hostname before comparing it with lower(host). URI parsing preserves hostname case, so an allowed entry such as example.com does not match https://EXAMPLE.com/page even though DNS hostnames are case-insensitive. This makes valid embedding requests fail the host authorization check and makes category lookup inconsistent for equivalent domain identities. Compare against host.downcase (or normalize both operands equivalently), and add a mixed-case URL test.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Guard the empty query result before indexing row 0. If embed_category has no stored setting or its value does not match an existing category name, the join returns zero rows and `[0]['id']` raises rather than reaching the uncategorized fallback below. This aborts the migration even for sites that have never configured embedding. Retrieve the first row safely and use the uncategorized category when no row is returned.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The category lookup assumes the SELECT returns a row: `[0]['id']` raises when embed_category has never been configured or its category no longer exists. This happens before the `category_id == 0` fallback, so ordinary installations without an embedding setting cannot run this migration. Handle an empty result explicitly and resolve the uncategorized fallback safely as well (its SELECT also assumes a stored setting row).

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The before_validation callback calls `sub!` on host without guarding nil. Creating a host with a missing or null host field reaches this callback from save_host and raises NoMethodError instead of returning a validation error. Guard nil during normalization and let presence/format validation reject it.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Normalize legacy host entries before inserting them. The previous host-setting contract accepted values such as `http://discourse.org` and `https://example.com/1234` (both appear in the previous embedding tests), but `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` now compares only the parsed hostname against the stored column. These direct SQL inserts bypass the model's scheme/path-stripping callback, leaving those existing entries as full URLs. After upgrading, EmbedController and TopicRetriever reject embedding from previously allowed sites. Apply the same normalization when migrating legacy values.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The test named "is false if embeddable_host is blank" now uses an ordinary built topic without setting embed_truncate or making has_topic_embed? true. It therefore returns false for reasons unrelated to the missing host, and passes even with the new implementation that never checks host availability. If blank-host behavior remains the intended contract, arrange all the other prerequisites before asserting false; if the contract intentionally changed, replace this case with a test of the actual intended behavior rather than retaining a misleading passing test.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: This test now requests fruit 2 but expects fruit 1's two colors. The /fruits/:id Pretender handler always returns fruits[0], so the test passes while hydrating the wrong record and would not catch a find implementation that ignores the requested ID. Make the handler select the requested fruit and assert its ID and corresponding colors (fruit 2 has only color 3), or request fruit 1 if testing its two-color hydration is the goal.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The category query can return no rows when embed_category has not been explicitly stored or does not match a category name. In that case `[0]` is nil and `['id']` raises before the `category_id == 0` fallback can run, preventing migration even on sites that never configured embedding. Check for an empty result before extracting the ID.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The validator accepts hosts such as `example.com:8080`, but record_for_host extracts only URI.host (`example.com`) and compares it to the stored port-qualified string. An accepted and saved host therefore never authorizes its corresponding URLs. Normalize the stored and queried authority consistently, including a deliberate port policy.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: When categoryId is null (the default for a new row, or a cleared selection), the controller saves SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id and returns that category_id. This callback instead overwrites host.category with findById(null), making the displayed category disagree with the saved category. Use the category from the save response or its returned category_id rather than the pre-save selection.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Normalize migrated host values to the same bare-host representation used by EmbeddableHost before inserting them. This SQL bypasses the new model's before_validation normalization and copies values such as `http://discourse.org` or `https://example.com/1234` verbatim. The replacement record_for_host lookup compares URI.host (e.g. `discourse.org`) to the stored string, so previously configured scheme/path-prefixed hosts stop being authorized after upgrade.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Use the saved response's category rather than overwriting it from categoryId after saving. For a new host with no category selected, categoryId is null, while the new controller deliberately saves SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id and returns that ID through the serializer. This callback replaces the hydrated category with findById(null), leaving the row without its actual category until reload (and reopening edit also initializes from that incorrect relationship).

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The flex-item styling targets the inner .extra-info-wrapper rather than the outer div generated by header-extra-info's Ember.Component. With .contents now using flexbox, that outer div retains its automatic minimum width, so a long nowrap topic title cannot shrink to the available space and pushes the navigation panel outside the header instead of being ellipsized by the existing desktop truncation rules. Move the extra-info-wrapper class onto the component's root element and set min-width: 0 on that flex item so ordering and truncation apply to the actual header child.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The alignment mixin does not match the Mozilla fallback emitted by flexbox(): when display: -moz-box is selected, neither align-items nor the WebKit/MS declarations control its cross-axis alignment. Consequently @include align-items(center) in the header and small-action leaves those children at the legacy default instead of vertically centering them. Emit -moz-box-align: $alignment alongside -webkit-box-align so the advertised fallback produces the same alignment.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The second self.downsize definition replaces the existing width/height definition rather than overloading it in Ruby. Jobs::ResizeEmoji.execute still calls downsize(path, path, 100, 100, opts), so emoji resizing now raises ArgumentError instead of resizing. Use a single method that supports both argument forms, or give the geometry-string method a distinct name.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Passing the multipart tempfile path to downsize prevents animation detection when that path does not end in .gif, even when allow_animated_thumbnails is enabled. OptimizedImage.optimize checks the path suffix and otherwise uses convert with input[0], so oversized animated GIF uploads are permanently flattened to their first frame. Preserve the original image extension in the processing path or pass the image format explicitly to select animated processing.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The fixed 10 MB client limit is applied to attachments as well as images, replacing max_attachment_size_kb. Sites configured to allow attachments larger than 10 MB can no longer upload those valid files through the composer, although UploadValidator still permits them. Apply the new input ceiling only to images and retain the configured attachment limit.

suggestions.label: performance
suggestions.suggestionContent: The retry loop ignores downsize's false return value and retries failed conversions while the file remains oversized. convert_with returns false on converter failure, so an unsupported or malformed oversized image launches the same failing external conversion up to five times per upload without any changed input. Break on a failed downsize result and return an upload error rather than repeating the conversion.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Ruby does not overload methods by argument count: this second downsize definition replaces the width/height version above it. Existing callers such as app/jobs/regular/resize_emoji.rb:14 still call downsize(path, path, 100, 100, opts), which now raises ArgumentError (five arguments for a method accepting three to four), breaking emoji resizing. Use a separate method name for the geometry-string variant or one method that explicitly supports both calling conventions.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Ruby does not overload methods by arity: this second downsize definition replaces the width/height version above it. The existing consumer in app/jobs/regular/resize_emoji.rb:14 still invokes OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, 100, 100, opts), so emoji resizing now fails with ArgumentError (five arguments supplied, three to four expected). Preserve compatibility through a single argument-dispatching method, or update that consumer to pass a geometry string and remove the overwritten definition.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Ruby does not overload methods by arity: this second `downsize` definition replaces the five-argument version above it. The existing call in `app/jobs/regular/resize_emoji.rb:14`, `OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, 100, 100, opts)`, consequently raises ArgumentError instead of resizing the emoji. Preserve both calling conventions through a single argument-dispatching method, or give the dimensions-string variant a distinct name and update its new caller.

suggestions.label: compatibility
suggestions.suggestionContent: Duplicate downsize definitions pose a compatibility concern for older callers: the final definition accepts a percentage geometry string and an options hash, potentially replacing the definition expected by those callers. This issue is visible within the model hunk, rather than being a disagreement between changed files.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: totalPages counts an extra page whenever user_count is an exact multiple of limit. With 50 members and limit 50, the UI displays two pages and enables Next to request offset 50, which returns an empty member list. Use Math.ceil(user_count / limit) while retaining the zero-member guard.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The public members route now loads only the model's default 50-member page without providing any way to request subsequent pages. The public group/members.hbs template only renders members and has no Next/Previous controls, so members after the first 50 become inaccessible (manual groups previously returned all members). Add public pagination controls and actions that update offset and reload members.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Removing a member with group.users.delete bypasses the primary_group_id cleanup previously performed by Group#destroy_deletions during usernames updates. A user whose primary group is this group remains associated with it as their primary group after membership removal, leaving stale primary-group state used by user administration and post serialization. Clear primary_group_id for the removed user when it equals this group's id as part of the removal operation.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The new default limit applies to nonautomatic groups as well, but the public group-members route still calls findMembers() only once and its template simply iterates members without pagination. Previously this endpoint returned every member of a nonautomatic group; now a group with more than 50 members exposes only the first 50 on its public members page, with no way to reach the rest. Update that consumer to fetch subsequent pages or provide pagination when introducing this endpoint contract.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Use Math.ceil(user_count / limit) for the page count. Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1 adds a nonexistent page whenever the member count is an exact positive multiple of the limit. For example, 50 members with limit 50 yields 2 pages, so showingLast is false on the only populated page and Next fetches offset 50, displaying an empty member list.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Guard against stale member-fetch responses before updating the model. `next` updates offset immediately and leaves navigation enabled, so with at least three pages two rapid clicks issue requests for offsets 50 and 100. If the offset-100 response arrives first and the offset-50 response arrives last, this unconditional `setProperties` resets both offset and members to the older page, undoing the latest navigation. Refreshes after membership changes can similarly be overwritten by an earlier fetch. Track a per-model request generation and apply only the latest response, or serialize navigation and refresh requests.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Use Math.ceil(user_count / limit) for totalPages. With exactly 50 members and a limit of 50, this reports two pages and enables Next, which fetches offset 50 and displays an empty page. Every positive exact multiple of the page size has this off-by-one error.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Persist params[:alias_level] when creating a group, just as update does. The creation form exposes aliasLevelOptions and group.asJSON sends the selected alias_level, but create saves only name and visible. A newly created group therefore retains the default alias level instead of the administrator's selection.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Provide pagination or load subsequent pages for the public group-members view. findMembers now requests only 50 members, and this route calls it only once while its template simply iterates members without navigation. Custom groups previously returned all members, so groups larger than 50 now have members that cannot be viewed on this page.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The public member list now renders only the first page. GroupsController#members now limits all groups to 50 members by default, and Group.findMembers stores only that page in members; the public group-members route fetches it once. This template renders the partial array without the pagination controls/actions added to the admin view, leaving members beyond the first 50 inaccessible (including custom groups that previously returned all members). Add public pagination or otherwise fetch the remaining pages rather than treating members as the complete list.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The new fallback order depends on SiteSetting.default_locale, but the accelerator's translation cache does not include that setting or the current site in its key. In a multisite process, two sites with the same user locale and different default locales reuse the first site's cached fallback translation; changing the default locale also leaves cached fallback results stale. Include the effective fallback chain or site/default-locale context in the translation cache key.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Fallback catalogs are ensured loaded only in the controller filter, leaving non-controller translation paths without the catalogs required by the newly enabled fallback backend. Jobs::Base sets I18n.locale directly and PostAlerter uses I18n.with_locale, while the accelerator loads only the current locale and backend fallback lookups bypass that loader; missing keys therefore still produce missing translations or skip the configured site fallback until another request happens to load those catalogs. Ensure the full fallback chain is loaded at the translation boundary, rather than relying solely on the controller filter.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: The new authentication gate accepts retries from devices that were rejected by the limit because tagDeviceUI inserts the cache entry before CreateOrUpdateDevice succeeds. At capacity, the first request with a new X-Grafana-Device-Id fails, but subsequent requests with that same ID hit the 29-minute cache and receive an anonymous identity without admission to the device store. Cache only successful admissions, and ensure concurrent requests cannot treat an in-progress admission as successful.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: The device-limit authentication gate treats requests without X-Grafana-Device-Id as admitted because TagDevice returns nil immediately for an empty header. A client can omit this client-controlled header and obtain an anonymous identity even when the configured device limit is full. When a positive limit is configured, require a valid device identifier or supply an enforced server-side identification mechanism before granting anonymous access.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The device count check and subsequent upsert are not atomic. With one remaining slot, concurrent requests for different device IDs can both observe a count below the limit and both insert, exceeding the configured maximum; the unique device_id index does not serialize admissions for different IDs. Serialize admission across instances using a database-backed lock or equivalent atomic quota operation encompassing the count and write.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The new device_limit setting is read without adding a corresponding key to conf/defaults.ini. applyEnvVariableOverrides only visits keys already present in the loaded INI and runs before readAuthSettings, so setting GF_AUTH_ANONYMOUS_DEVICE_LIMIT alone is ignored and leaves the limit at zero, disabling enforcement. Add an uncommented device_limit = 0 entry under auth.anonymous in defaults.ini so the standard environment override mechanism can apply it.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Propagating the limit error is not enough to enforce the limit: tagDeviceUI sets localCache before CreateOrUpdateDevice runs. When persistence returns ErrDeviceLimitReached, the rejected device remains cached for 29 minutes; its next request returns nil from the cache hit and Authenticate grants anonymous access. Cache only successfully persisted devices, or remove the cache entry on failure, so retrying cannot bypass the limit.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The capacity check and subsequent device insertion are not atomic. If the count is one below deviceLimit, two concurrent requests for different new devices can both observe that count and both insert successfully, exceeding the configured limit. Serialize capacity checking and insertion with appropriate database locking or an equivalent atomic admission mechanism, including across Grafana instances.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Propagating the limit error leaves a successful-tag marker in the local cache: tagDeviceUI sets the cache entry before CreateOrUpdateDevice runs. When the store returns ErrDeviceLimitReached, the first request fails, but a retry from the same device hits that entry and returns nil without checking the store, allowing anonymous authentication despite the limit for the cache lifetime. Cache only successfully admitted devices, or remove the entry on failure, and ensure concurrent cache hits cannot treat an in-progress admission as successful.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The count check and subsequent upsert are not an atomic admission operation. With one slot remaining, two concurrent requests for different new device IDs can both read count < deviceLimit and then both insert, exceeding the configured limit. This also occurs across Grafana instances sharing the database. Serialize admission using a database-level locking/transaction strategy that protects the count and write together; an ordinary transaction without appropriate locking/isolation is insufficient. Add a concurrent distinct-device test.

suggestions.label: performance
suggestions.suggestionContent: The cache is not rechecked after acquiring the write lock, so concurrent production requests that initially observe a nil cache each reload and decode the manifest even after another request has populated it. During a cold-start request burst, these redundant filesystem reads and JSON decodes execute serially under the global lock, delaying queued page and frontend-settings requests and blocking cache readers while each reload runs. After acquiring the write lock, return the populated cache when cfg.Env != setting.Dev before performing asset loading.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The metric help text describes sizes "returned", but the observations measure incoming payloads: QueryData sums len(v.JSON) and CallResource uses len(req.Body), both before invoking the plugin. This description exposes request sizes as though they were response sizes to operators reading Prometheus metadata. Change the help text to describe incoming plugin request payload sizes.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The millisecond observations truncate the duration before converting it to float64: elapsed/time.Millisecond is integer division. For example, a 900µs request is recorded as 0ms and a 1.9ms request as 1ms, misclassifying observations against the fractional millisecond buckets declared above and understating the histogram sum. Use float64(elapsed)/float64(time.Millisecond) in both the exemplar and ordinary observation paths to preserve the actual duration.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The request-size cases pass an empty Body and no Queries, and subsequently check only that a histogram sample exists. Replacing either size calculation with a constant zero still passes this test. Use nonempty resource bodies and query JSON payloads and assert the histogram sample sum equals their expected byte count, so broken request-size instrumentation is detected.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Both duration metrics are checked only for labels and a nonzero sample count. Observing a constant zero, or feeding seconds into the milliseconds metric, still passes. Assert the observed durations using a controlled elapsed interval (or check the relationship between the two histogram sums with allowance for millisecond truncation) so the test detects broken duration values and units.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The asynchronous legacy write derives its timeout context from the request context, which is canceled when the HTTP request finishes. Create, Update, Delete, and DeleteCollection return before this work completes, so their legacy database operations can be canceled immediately instead of receiving the intended ten-second window. Derive the bounded background context from context.WithoutCancel(ctx) to retain request values without inheriting request cancellation.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Legacy.Update receives the original objInfo instead of the object successfully committed to unified storage. The playlist legacy implementation calls objInfo.UpdatedObject(ctx, old) against its own legacy object, so a patch is reapplied to potentially stale state and can persist a different result or fail rather than mirror the unified write. Pass an updateWrapper containing res, as the previous implementation did.

suggestions.label: performance
suggestions.suggestionContent: Successful Delete passes the resource name into the histogram's kind label. metrics.go retains a separate HistogramVec child for every distinct label set, so deleting uniquely named resources continuously grows process memory and exported metric cardinality. Pass options.Kind instead of name.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The legacy DeleteCollection duration and error status are recorded in the unified-storage histogram. Every successful unified deletion therefore produces a second storage observation for a different backend, while legacy deletion failures are attributed to unified storage and no legacy observation is emitted. Call recordLegacyDuration here instead.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The test name says creation happens "only in the unified store", but this case configures a successful Legacy.Create as well, and Mode3.Create launches that legacy write after the unified write succeeds. Rename the case to describe creation in both stores (with the legacy write asynchronous), so test output does not communicate the opposite of the mode-3 write contract.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The successful Create test never verifies the legacy write. Configuring m.On("Create", ...) does not require that expectation to be consumed, and these assertions only inspect the object returned by Storage.Create. Deleting the entire legacy-create goroutine would still pass this test. Use distinct storage and legacy mocks and synchronize on the legacy call, then assert that it completed with the intended object.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The successful Update case configures a legacy Update expectation but returns after checking only the unified-store result. It neither waits for the asynchronous legacy update nor verifies its expectation, so removing the legacy-update goroutine entirely still passes. Add explicit synchronization and verification of the legacy update (ideally with separate mocks), including the object propagated to legacy storage.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The legacy write is now asynchronous but still inherits the caller's request context. Once Create returns and the HTTP request completes, that context is canceled; WithTimeoutCause does not detach parent cancellation. Legacy.Create can therefore fail with context canceled despite a successful unified-store write. The same lifetime mismatch affects the new Update, Delete, and DeleteCollection goroutines. Detach cancellation while retaining request values before launching background work (and apply the bounded timeout to that context), or keep the writes synchronous.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Legacy.Update previously received an updateWrapper containing the object returned by Storage.Update; it now receives the original objInfo. UpdatedObjectInfo can compute an update from the old object supplied by each backend (notably for patches), so evaluating it against a stale legacy object can produce a different result or reject an update that already succeeded in Storage. Preserve the canonical-result contract by passing an updateWrapper with updated: res and upstream: objInfo to the legacy consumer rather than replaying the original update against legacy state.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The failing operation is d.Storage.Create, but its duration/error is recorded through recordLegacyDuration. Use recordStorageDuration here so storage create failures are not counted as legacy failures while disappearing from storage error metrics.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: This branch handles d.Storage.Update failing, yet records a Legacy duration/error. Use recordStorageDuration to attribute the elapsed time and failure to the backend actually called.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The timed call is d.Legacy.DeleteCollection, but its measurement is emitted using recordStorageDuration. Use recordLegacyDuration; otherwise storage receives two measurements for a successful collection deletion and legacy receives none, and legacy failures appear as storage failures.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The successful Storage.Delete measurement passes name instead of options.Kind, unlike the error path and other operation measurements. Use options.Kind consistently; successful and failed deletes otherwise land in different label series, with successful deletes split by individual object name.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The background legacy write derives its timeout context from the request context. Returning from the HTTP handler cancels that parent, so a legacy write that has not finished (or has not even started) receives cancellation despite the nominal ten-second timeout. Storage has already committed and the caller receives success, leaving legacy state missing or stale. Detach cancellation while preserving context values before launching background work, then apply the bounded timeout. The same issue affects Update, Delete and DeleteCollection.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Independent goroutines remove ordering between successful writes to the same resource. For example, Storage commits update A and then update B, but the legacy goroutine for B can finish before A, leaving legacy with A while Storage contains B. Likewise a delete can run before an earlier create and leave a resurrected legacy object. Preserve per-resource commit order for mirroring (including across create/update/delete), rather than launching each write independently.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Legacy.Update now receives the original objInfo rather than the updateWrapper containing the object successfully committed to Storage. UpdatedObjectInfo can represent a patch/transform based on the supplied old object; replaying it against legacy's potentially different old state can persist a different result or fail, even though the authoritative update succeeded. suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Locking only cache publication allows concurrent requests for the same uncached key to build separate indexes and overwrite each other's cache entries. suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The new startup log calls TotalDocs after launching the write-event listener, but bleveBackend.TotalDocs iterates b.cache without cacheMu.RLock. suggestions.label: bug

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Make skipToken return neutral [false, false] abilities rather than forwarding undefined to useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities. suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Preserve the federated-group immutability check when delegating this CombinedRule hook. suggestions.label: bug

suggestions.suggestionContent: Hard-coding isFederated=false now also affects useAllAlertRuleAbilities, which delegates to this helper after the refactor.
