suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The new grant metadata falls back to 'na' for client-credentials and UMA tokens because their issuance paths never set Constants.GRANT_TYPE on their fresh ClientSessionContext. ClientCredentialsGrantType calls responseBuilder.generateAccessToken directly, and PermissionGrantType delegates to AuthorizationTokenService, so neither executes the new assignment in createTokenResponse; tokens from these known grants therefore carry unknown grant context. Set the grant attribute in both issuance paths before generating the access token.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The access-token ID matcher extracts substring(3, 5) instead of substring(4, 6) and returns false when the extracted value equals the expected grant. This allows tokens with incorrect grant shortcuts to pass the authorization-code, refresh, device and CIBA event assertions, while malformed short prefixes can throw instead of producing a mismatch. Require a six-character prefix and reject when !items[0].substring(4, 6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut).

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Grant shortcuts are registered without enforcing the two-character length required by the decoder. A custom grant returning a three-character shortcut, which the new OAuth2GrantTypeFactory documentation explicitly suggests, produces a seven-character prefix that getTokenContextFromTokenId rejects, breaking encode/decode round trips for that grant. Validate shortcut length during registration and dynamic refresh, and document the required two-character format.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The rawTokenId null check validates grantType a second time instead of rawTokenId. A context constructed with a null raw ID is accepted and encodeTokenId serializes it as the literal 'null', violating the constructor's non-null invariant and losing the token identifier. Pass rawTokenId to this Objects.requireNonNull call.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The event matcher does not follow the new token-ID contract. The encoder places the grant shortcut at indices [4, 6), but this consumer reads [3, 5) and returns false when it equals the expected shortcut rather than when it differs. Consequently, for example, expectCodeToToken accepts `onrtrt:<valid UUID>` even though that is a refresh-token grant instead of an authorization-code grant. Check the prefix length and reject when `!items[0].substring(4, 6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)` so the updated event assertions actually validate the grant.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The new contract describes getShortcut() as usually returning a three-letter shortcut, but DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider requires exactly two characters for the grant field (six total prefix characters, decoded with substring(4, 6)). An extension author following this documentation can produce token IDs that the default decoder rejects. Document the required two-character length rather than advertising three letters.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The expectedGrantShortcut parameter and accompanying comment promise validation of the expected grant, but this implementation extracts substring(3, 5) and returns false on equality. The encoder places the grant at zero-based positions 4–5, so typical IDs with any grant pass this check, contradicting the matcher’s expected-grant contract and allowing incorrect grant context to pass the new event assertions. Compare substring(4, 6) with the expected shortcut and reject inequality (after validating prefix length).

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The grant assertion uses substring(3, 5) and rejects equality. The encoder places the grant at indices 4–5, so this matcher generally accepts any grant prefix with a UUID suffix. For example, an authorization-code event containing `onrtna:<uuid>` still passes the expected `ac` check. Validate the prefix length and return false when substring(4, 6) does not equal expectedGrantShortcut.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Catching RuntimeException allows this negative test to pass for an unrelated fixture failure. The fixture constructs the factory without postInit, leaving sessionFactory null; resolving the unregistered `ac` shortcut calls sessionFactory.getProviderFactoriesStream and throws NullPointerException before the decoder's intended unknown-grant IllegalArgumentException. Catch/assert IllegalArgumentException specifically and provide a factory fixture whose lookup returns no matching grant, so removing the decoder's validation would fail the test.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The grant segment is at indices [4,6), not [3,5). For example, `onrtac:<uuid>` yields `ta` here rather than `ac`, preventing the matcher from actually checking the encoded grant. Extract `substring(4,6)` (after checking the prefix length) to match the encoder layout.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The equality condition is inverted: it returns false when the extracted grant equals the expected grant and accepts mismatches. Independently of correcting the slice indices, negate this equality check so that wrong-grant token IDs fail and correct-grant IDs pass.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The encoder places the grant shortcut at indices 4–6, but this matcher reads substring(3, 5) and returns false on equality. Consequently a token with the wrong grant normally passes the assertion as long as its suffix is a UUID. Require substring(4, 6) to equal expectedGrantShortcut (and validate prefix length before slicing).

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The check labelled 'Null rawTokenId not allowed' validates grantType a second time instead of rawTokenId. A null raw ID is accepted and encodeTokenId subsequently emits the literal suffix ':null'. Validate rawTokenId here to enforce the declared invariant.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The new shortcut contract recommends three-letter shortcuts, but getTokenContextFromTokenId requires a six-character prefix and consumes exactly two grant characters. A custom grant following this contract produces a seven-character prefix that the decoder rejects. Specify exactly two characters and enforce that constraint when registering shortcuts, or change the encoding/decoding format to support the documented lengths.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Validate that every grant shortcut is exactly two characters before registering it. The new OAuth2GrantTypeFactory contract explicitly describes three-letter shortcuts, and encodeTokenId accepts them unchanged, but getTokenContextFromTokenId requires a six-character prefix and slices only two characters for the grant. A custom grant following that contract therefore produces tokens that this provider cannot decode (IllegalArgumentException). Apply the same validation to lazy registration.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Enforce shortcut uniqueness during lazy registration rather than overwriting grantsByShortcuts. If a newly deployed grant B uses existing grant A's shortcut, this path replaces shortcut→A with shortcut→B while retaining both forward entries. Previously issued A tokens then decode as B. Concurrent registrations of two new grants with the same shortcut likewise both succeed, with the last inverse-map write winning. Use collision-aware atomic registration and reject the conflicting grant before publishing its forward mapping.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The rawTokenId null validation checks grantType again. Passing a null rawTokenId therefore creates a context despite the declared non-null constraint, and encodeTokenId silently emits the literal suffix ':null'. Check rawTokenId here so invalid token IDs are rejected at construction.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The encoder produces a prefix consisting of two session characters, two token characters, and two grant characters (for example `onrtac`), but this matcher reads substring(3, 5) and rejects equality instead of requiring it. Thus expectCodeToToken/expectRefresh/etc. accept token IDs with the wrong grant, hiding failures in the grant-context propagation this PR introduces. Validate a six-character prefix and require substring(4, 6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut).

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The new getShortcut contract describes a shortcut as usually three letters, but DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider requires an exactly six-character context prefix and reads only two characters for the grant. A custom grant implementing the documented three-letter shortcut will issue token IDs that this decoder rejects, so encoding and decoding cannot round-trip for a conforming extension. Specify exactly two characters in this contract and enforce that constraint when registering shortcuts, or change the encoding format to support the documented variable length.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The test asserts caughtExceptions without waiting for the reader thread to finish its in-flight request. A concurrent read can fail and append its exception after the empty assertion has passed, allowing the regression test to pass despite the server error it is intended to detect. Keep a reference to the reader thread, signal it to stop, and join it before asserting the collected exceptions.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The reader's stop flag is set only after every deletion succeeds, with no finally block. If any remove() throws, the test exits with a live non-daemon thread that keeps issuing requests and collecting exceptions indefinitely, interfering with teardown and potentially preventing JVM termination. Put stop signaling and reader termination in a finally block around deletion.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Wait for the reader thread to finish before asserting caughtExceptions is empty. Setting deletedAll only prevents another loop iteration; an already-running groups request can fail and append its exception after this assertion, causing the regression test to pass despite a concurrent-read error. Keep the thread reference and join it before inspecting the results.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Wait for the reader thread to finish before asserting caughtExceptions. A reader can enter the groups request before the final deletion, while the main thread completes deletion, sets deletedAll and asserts an empty list. If that in-flight request then fails, its exception is added after the assertion and the test incorrectly passes. Keep the Thread reference and join it before checking the results.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Stop the reader in a finally block. If any remove() call throws, execution never reaches deletedAll.set(true), leaving the newly started non-daemon thread continuously issuing requests even after this test fails and the realm is cleaned up. Ensure the flag is set and the worker is awaited on the exceptional path as well.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The exception assertion runs without waiting for the reader thread to finish. Setting deletedAll only prevents a subsequent loop iteration; a request already in flight can throw and append to caughtExceptions after assertThat has passed. The reader can also first be scheduled after deletedAll is true and perform no reads at all. Thus this regression test can pass with the original concurrent-deletion null dereference restored. Retain the reader thread, coordinate its startup/read activity with deletion, and join it before asserting the collected failures.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The diagnostic suffix scan can overlap the already matched prefix, producing an invalid substring range. For example, an unclosed outer tag in `x` is repaired to `x`, so the prefix consumes the original string while the suffix still matches ``, throwing StringIndexOutOfBoundsException instead of returning validation errors. Bound the suffix scan by each string's remaining length after subtracting start.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The English multivalued-size message now uses Java MessageFormat placeholders and choice syntax although the account UI translates it with i18next. PersonalInfo passes numeric parameters through setUserProfileServerError to t(), and the unchanged i18next configuration expects double-brace interpolation, so users see literal `{0}`, `{1}`, `{2}` and the choice expression; the same regression exists in the admin UI message at line 3138. suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The Lithuanian OTP setup instruction has been replaced with an Italian sentence. login-config-totp.ftl renders this message directly, so users selecting Lithuanian receive an instruction in the wrong language; the same copied sentence also appears in the Lithuanian account bundle at line 101. Replace both values with the Lithuanian translation of the new installation instruction.

suggestions.suggestionContent: Choice normalization removes all branch content before HTML validation, allowing prohibited markup to bypass the new translation policy. A translated error-invalid-multivalued-size value such as `{2,choice,0#values|1#value|1

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The replacement OTP setup instruction is Italian (“Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare”), but this is the Lithuanian locale and the surrounding setup steps are Lithuanian. Translate the new instruction into Lithuanian rather than copying the Italian translation. The same replacement was made for `totpStep1` in the Lithuanian account bundle. suggestions.suggestionContent: Bound the suffix scan by the unmatched length remaining after `start`. For example, an English value `x` selects POLICY_SOME_HTML and sanitizes to `x`. suggestions.suggestionContent: Bound the suffix scan by the remaining length after the matching prefix, rather than by each full string length. The current scans can overlap: sanitizing 'x' to 'x' yields start=8 and end=4, making both diagnostic substring ranges inverted. suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: The global VIEW check returns true before evaluating client-specific VIEW permissions, bypassing a negative permission on an individual client. An administrator granted VIEW on all clients can therefore read a client explicitly excluded by a client-specific denial; ClientsResource.getClients also bypasses per-client checks when this evaluator's parameterless canView() returns true. Evaluate the specific client resource before falling back to the all-clients permission, and ensure listing does not use a global grant to skip specific denials.

suggestions.label: performance
suggestions.suggestionContent: canView() does not recognize an all-clients MANAGE permission even though canView(client) grants viewing through canConfigure(client) and canManage(client). For an administrator with global MANAGE but no VIEW, ClientsResource.getClients selects an unpaginated realm-wide client stream and evaluates authorization for clients before applying pagination, instead of fetching the requested database page. Include the global MANAGE permission in the global viewing capability while preserving client-specific denial semantics.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The new Javadoc says requireView() returns true, but its declaration returns void. Describe normal completion when canView() succeeds and ForbiddenException when it fails, as the neighbouring require-method documentation does, so callers are not given a nonexistent boolean return contract.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: requireViewClientScopes() is void, so the new statement that it returns true is incorrect. Document it as a guard that throws ForbiddenException when canViewClientScopes() is false rather than as a boolean predicate.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Do not short-circuit resource-specific view evaluation on the global fine-grained VIEW grant. With an all-clients VIEW permission allowing an administrator and a client-specific VIEW permission denying that administrator, canView() returns true here and the specific client permission is never evaluated. This differs from the specific-over-global override behavior exercised for users in this PR and exposes the denied client's representation. Keep the administrative-role bypass separate from fine-grained grants and evaluate the client's resource before falling back to the all-clients resource; also ensure the global view result used by client listing cannot bypass those overrides.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The expected ForbiddenException can come from getDefaultClientScopes(), before removeDefaultClientScope() is invoked. With no permission granted, the initial read is forbidden, so this test still passes if removal's manage-permission check is removed entirely; the later granted removal also succeeds in that broken implementation. Obtain the scope ID using the privileged realm client outside this try block, then invoke only removeDefaultClientScope() through the restricted client and assert that it is forbidden.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: PasswordForm.configuredFor now accepts passkey-only users even when the active login theme renders the unchanged base login-password.ftl, which contains no passkeys UI. The legacy keycloak theme inherits that template, so a user without a password reaches a password-only challenge with no way to authenticate instead of being able to use the newly accepted passkey credential. Add the passkeys import and conditionalUIData invocation to the base login-password.ftl as well as the keycloak.v2 override.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The early return compares the original IDP's organization-aware enabled state rather than the persisted enabled state used to populate the login cache. If a cached public IDP's organization is disabled and an admin changes BROKER_PUBLIC to false, the original predicate is false because the organization is disabled and the updated predicate is false because the broker is private, so the stale ID remains cached; re-enabling the organization displays the now-private broker because the login bean only rechecks isEnabled. Compare raw persisted models for login-cache invalidation, for example by loading the original through idpDelegate.getById before applying this predicate.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The cleanup callback removes the literal IDP alias "alias" instead of the newly created "idp-alias-" + i; the same mistake occurs for idp-alias-20 at line 425. TestCleanup.addCleanup suppresses the resulting deletion exceptions, leaving the created providers in the shared test realm and contaminating subsequent tests or repeated runs. Register cleanup with idpRep.getAlias(), or use getCleanup().addIdentityProviderAlias(idpRep.getAlias()), at both creation sites.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Consume and assert the results of getForLogin, including a repeat query for the same mode/organization to exercise a cache hit. All calls in this test discard the returned stream and assert only IdentityProviderListQuery contents. The implementation populates that query before reconstructing the returned models, so returning an empty stream (or the wrong providers) at line 254 would still pass the entire test. Assert the expected provider identities on both the initial query and the cached query, rather than only the internal cached count.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Do not merge the previously read query into a newly revisioned entry without verifying its revision. A reader can obtain a query containing organization A's IDs, then another transaction disables a provider or changes its organization and invalidates this key. When the reader requests an uncached organization B, this branch obtains a fresh revision but copies the old A results into the new query and publishes it using the current counter. Subsequent A requests receive stale membership indefinitely (a disabled or moved provider still exists, so the null-ID fallback does not repair it). Rebuild rather than copy after invalidation, or ensure the old query's revision is still valid atomically before publishing the merged entry.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The cleanup targets the literal alias "alias", but this loop creates providers named "idp-alias-" + i. Consequently cleanup attempts to remove a different/nonexistent provider and leaves the created providers behind, potentially failing teardown or contaminating subsequent tests. Capture each actual created alias for its cleanup callback. The same mismatch occurs for the separately created idp-alias-20 at line 425.

suggestions.suggestionContent: Include the organization slug or ID in this query key. The query function fetches `/organizations/${organization.slug}/trace-items/attributes/`, but the key contains only query options. Two organizations with the same project selection (especially the all-projects selection), date range and dataset therefore share a cache entry. Switching organizations can display the previous organization's attributes, and overlapping requests can populate the shared entry with the wrong organization's result.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Check field presence rather than truthiness when enforcing timestamp/age exclusivity. A report containing both `timestamp: 0` and `age: 0` passes both validators, despite the declared constraint that they must not coexist; with only one zero value, validation is also asymmetric. Use membership checks on initial_data (or object-level validation) and add zero-value mixed-field tests.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: Include the organization slug in this query key. The request function fetches attributes for the current organization, but the cache key only contains dataset/type, date range, and project selection. Switching organizations with the same filters (for example an all-projects selection) reuses the same cache entry and can display the previous organization's custom attribute names in the new organization's Explore UI. The previous endpoint-based key included the organization slug and isolated these results.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: Do not attach the complete raw report to the validation warning. Browser reports contain page URLs (potentially including tokens or personal data in query strings) and arbitrary body contents. Any invalid field now causes that entire payload to be emitted at warning level, exposing it in operational logs even where the existing info-level request logging is filtered out. Log the failed field names/report type or a redacted diagnostic instead.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The feature-enabled branch ignores `result.data`, `result.meta`, and the computed fields and instead passes empty columns and empty data. TableWidgetVisualization consumes these props directly, so every dashboard table becomes empty for organizations with `use-table-widget-visualization`, even when the query returned rows. Pass the actual result and corresponding columns rather than placeholder arrays.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The new query key contains only filter options, whereas the query function requests an organization-specific URL. Two organizations with identical project/date/type selections now share one cache entry (especially with the all-projects selection), allowing cached attribute keys from the previous organization to appear in the next one. Include the organization slug in the query key, as the previous URL-based key did.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: These validators check truthiness rather than field presence. `age=0` is a valid report age and `timestamp=0` is explicitly allowed, so a report containing both fields with zero values passes both validators despite the mutually exclusive contract. Check whether the opposite key is present in initial_data (or enforce exclusivity in object-level validation), and add a both-zero test.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The new isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process) guard does not match the SpawnProcess instances created by self.mp_context.Process. When a worker hangs, the guard skips kill() and the replacement starts while the original worker remains alive, allowing overlapping flushing of the same shards if the original resumes and leaking hung workers. Check against multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess or self.mp_context.Process, and kill and join the old worker before replacing it.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: join() breaks out of the worker loop when the shared deadline expires, skipping cleanup for every remaining worker. If next_step.join consumes the timeout or an earlier worker exhausts it, remaining flushers can continue running after shutdown or partition reassignment. Use the deadline only to limit waiting and still terminate and reap every remaining process.

suggestions.label: performance
suggestions.suggestionContent: The new loop calls get_memory_info() once per flusher buffer even though SpansBuffer.get_memory_info delegates to iter_cluster_memory_usage(self.client), which fetches INFO for the entire Redis cluster regardless of assigned_shards. With P flusher processes and memory backpressure enabled, each submitted batch now performs P identical cluster-wide memory queries on the consumer thread instead of one, increasing Redis traffic and blocking ingestion. Fetch cluster memory information once from a single buffer.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The new docstring says this creates one process per shard, but workers are capped by max_processes and shards are distributed among them. In particular, the CLI default of 1 means all assigned shards share one process. Describe capped workers with potentially multiple shards per worker so callers do not rely on per-shard process isolation.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: An explicit max_processes=0 is treated as an omitted limit by `or`, so passing `--flusher-processes 0` starts one process per assigned shard instead of respecting or rejecting the supplied zero limit. The CLI accepts zero as an integer and the factory forwards it unchanged. Default only when max_processes is None, and explicitly validate that supplied process limits are positive so zero cannot silently enable potentially many workers.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The workers are created with get_context("spawn").Process, which produces SpawnProcess instances; these are not instances of multiprocessing.Process (the default-context Process class). Consequently this guard skips kill() for actual production workers. When a worker hangs, the replacement starts while the original remains alive and can resume flushing the same shards. Use multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess or the spawn-context Process class for the check, and fix the identical check in join() so shutdown also terminates surviving workers.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Workers created by multiprocessing.get_context("spawn").Process are SpawnProcess instances, not instances of the separate multiprocessing.Process class. Consequently this guard skips kill() for production workers. When a live worker exceeds max-unhealthy-seconds, the code starts a replacement and overwrites its handle while the original is still running. If the original resumes, both workers flush the same shards, and repeated hangs can exceed the configured process limit. Check against multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess (or explicitly distinguish threads) and stop the old worker before replacing it.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Do not break out of worker cleanup when the join deadline expires. If the first worker consumes the timeout, the next iteration breaks before terminating that worker or any subsequent workers. They may still be blocked in Redis or producer calls despite the shared stopped flag, leaving old workers running after strategy shutdown/reassignment. Apply the deadline only to waiting, and perform termination cleanup for every worker regardless of remaining time (using a type check that recognizes spawn-context workers).

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The assertion counts shard entries rather than verifying shard assignment. A broken distribution such as {0: [0, 1], 1: [0, 1]} still passes all assertions in this test while shards 2 and 3 are never flushed. Assert that the flattened mapping contains exactly the expected assigned shards, with no duplicates (and verify each worker's shard buffer uses that mapping), rather than only asserting a total of four.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The queued default is evaluated once when the module is imported, so every AssignmentSource created without an explicit timestamp shares the worker's import-time timestamp. Both inbound assignment and deassignment use from_integration without supplying queued, so their serialized context records the wrong queue time for all subsequent events. Use dataclasses.field(default_factory=timezone.now) to generate the timestamp per instance.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: test_from_dict_empty_array passes {} rather than an empty array. It therefore only tests missing required dictionary keys and would still pass if rejection of an array input were broken. Pass [] to exercise the named case (or rename this test to empty_dict if that is the intended contract).

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: `timezone.now()` is evaluated once at module import, so every AssignmentSource created without an explicit queued value reports the same worker-start timestamp, even for assignments queued hours later. This makes the serialized `queued` timestamp incorrect. Use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` so each source records its own creation time, and test creation at two different times.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: `timezone.now()` is evaluated once when this module is imported, so every AssignmentSource created without an explicit `queued` value carries the worker's import timestamp rather than the assignment's queue time. `from_integration()` always takes this default, and `to_dict()` propagates the stale timestamp into outbound task payloads; long-running workers therefore emit incorrect assignment metadata. Use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` so each instance receives its own creation timestamp.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: The OAuth state is pipeline.signature, which Pipeline.__init__ computes solely from pipeline view class names and therefore shares across all users and installation attempts. An attacker can obtain an OAuth code for their own GitHub account and send a callback using this known state to a victim with an active installation pipeline, binding the attacker's GitHub identity to the victim's flow instead of rejecting the forged callback. Generate a random per-attempt nonce, store it in pipeline state, and validate that nonce on the OAuth callback.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: The missing Integration branch advances the pipeline without verifying that github_authenticated_user installed the supplied installation_id. When the installation webhook has not created a record, or the local record was deleted, finish_pipeline calls build_integration using app credentials and attaches the installation without checking the OAuth user's access, allowing a user with another account's installation ID to bypass the new ownership check. Fail closed until trusted installer information is available and apply the ownership check before every successful next_step.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The new ownership check indexes integration.metadata['sender']['login'] even though GitHubIntegrationProvider.build_integration omits sender for normal pipeline-created integrations. Reconnecting an existing active integration without an OrganizationIntegration and without webhook-populated sender now raises KeyError and returns a server error rather than an installation failure. Handle missing sender explicitly and return the invalid-installation response when trusted installer metadata is unavailable.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The record-absent path advances the pipeline before checking whether the authenticated GitHub user installed this app. Installation IDs arrive from the request, and a missing Integration record (for example before the installation webhook is processed) does not establish ownership. As a result, this path can attach an installation belonging to a different GitHub user despite the new authenticity check. Verify the authenticated user's authorization for the installation before advancing in this branch too, rather than relying on the webhook-created record existing.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The token request is executed outside the try block. If GitHub's token endpoint is unavailable or the request fails with a connection/timeout error, safe_urlopen raises before the guarded response parsing is reached, and this new installation step returns an unhandled server error instead of the installation-failed response. Include the request itself in the error handling and handle the relevant transport exceptions.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The new check treats `metadata['sender']` as required, but the integration producer still only adds it when `state.get('sender')` is present, and the existing installation code explicitly supports metadata without sender. An active integration without an OrganizationIntegration and without this optional field reaches this branch and now raises KeyError instead of completing the previously supported setup (or returning the invalid-installation response). Handle missing sender explicitly with a safe failure or a verified migration/backfill rather than indexing the optional field.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The replacement assertion no longer verifies that a nonexistent installation is rejected: 'Invalid installation request.' is also returned for a state mismatch, missing access token, or missing authenticated login before GitHubInstallation is reached. This test can therefore pass with installation-not-found handling broken if the callback fails OAuth validation instead. Establish a successful OAuth exchange with the actual pipeline state and verify that the nonexistent installation lookup is reached and rejected, rather than accepting this shared authentication-error message alone.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Translate the short-message literals at their definition/call sites instead of calling `_(error_short)` on a variable. Django's message extraction cannot extract the default `"Invalid installation request."` or the plain-string arguments at the two call sites from this dynamic gettext invocation. The existing pending-deletion and already-installed messages previously appeared directly inside `_()`; this refactor removes their extraction sites, and the new default message cannot enter translation catalogs. Use a translated default and translated arguments, then place `error_short` directly into the payload so these user-facing errors remain localizable.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: Do not use pipeline.signature as OAuth state. It is a deterministic MD5 of the pipeline identifiers, not an unpredictable nonce tied to this user's authorization attempt (the tests reuse it across users). An attacker can know the expected state and submit a callback containing a code authorized under the attacker's GitHub account, defeating the OAuth login-CSRF protection and the intended binding to the installing user. Generate a cryptographically random per-attempt state, store it in the session/pipeline, and validate and consume it on callback.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: MetricAlertDetectorHandler now inherits four unimplemented abstract members from StatefulDetectorHandler, making the registered handler impossible to instantiate. Accessing detector.detector_handler for the metric_alert_fire type calls this class in models/detector.py:86 and raises TypeError instead of returning a handler, aborting process_detectors before evaluation. Implement the required stateful methods or retain a concrete DetectorHandler implementation returning an empty dictionary until metric-alert evaluation is implemented.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: MetricAlertDetectorHandler now inherits StatefulDetectorHandler but remains abstract: in the other changed file, StatefulDetectorHandler declares build_occurrence_and_event_data as an abstract method (and requires get_dedupe_value and get_group_key_values). This pass-only subclass cannot be instantiated, so obtaining a metric-alert detector handler raises TypeError instead of returning the previously usable no-op handler. Keep the concrete no-op DetectorHandler implementation until the stateful methods can be implemented, or implement the required stateful contract here.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Changing this pass-only handler to StatefulDetectorHandler makes it abstract: the base requires get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, and build_occurrence_and_event_data implementations. Instantiating the registered metric-alert handler now raises TypeError instead of returning the previous no-op evaluation results, breaking detector processing before evaluate runs. Keep a concrete no-op DetectorHandler returning an empty dict until the stateful methods are implemented, or implement all required abstract methods here.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Update evaluate's adjacent docstring to describe a dictionary keyed by DetectorGroupKey rather than a list of DetectorEvaluationResult. This change returns a dictionary and callers now consume .values(), but the documented return contract still tells readers to expect a list; iterating the documented result as a list would instead yield group keys.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Remove or revise the adjacent TODO saying this will become a stateful detector 'when we build that abstraction'. The class now inherits StatefulDetectorHandler, so the comment describes already-completed work as a future migration and misleads maintainers about which abstraction this handler uses.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The new occurrence builder accepts `value` but never incorporates or asserts it, so the occurrence tests cannot detect incorrect forwarding of the measured value to `build_occurrence_and_event_data`. For example, `test_state_results_multi_group` supplies 10 for group_2 but builds its expected occurrence with 6 and still passes. A regression that passes a constant or another group's measurement at the new production hook would therefore go unnoticed. Include the value in the mock occurrence's evidence and use the actual expected measurement, or assert the hook's arguments directly.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: MetricAlertDetectorHandler becomes abstract when switched to StatefulDetectorHandler: it implements neither the stateful extraction methods nor the newly required build_occurrence_and_event_data hook. Previously its evaluate implementation made it a concrete no-op handler. Accessing detector.detector_handler for the registered metric-alert type now raises TypeError during handler construction instead of returning a handler, breaking processing before evaluation. Keep the concrete no-op implementation until the required stateful methods are implemented, or implement all abstract methods in this subclass.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: A matching date override returns true before checking busy periods. Both fixed-host and loose-host callers pass calendar and booking conflicts in busy, so a host with an override is offered even when an existing booking overlaps the slot. Continue to the busy checks after validating the override instead of returning true.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The override bounds reject only non-overlapping slots rather than requiring the entire event to fit inside an override. A fixed host with a 10:00–11:00 override accepts a 10:30–11:30 event generated from another host's availability, despite being unavailable for its final half hour. Accept only when at least one override contains both slotStartTime and slotEndTime; this also avoids rejecting a slot merely because another interval on the same date does not overlap it.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The working-hours predicate rejects a slot if any interval on its weekday does not contain it. A split schedule of 09:00–12:00 and 13:00–17:00 therefore loses every slot, since each valid slot lies outside the other interval. Require at least one matching interval to contain the full event instead of finding an interval that excludes it.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: A weekday with no matching working-hours entry falls through to the busy checks and is treated as available when there are no conflicts. In round-robin events, slots generated for a loose host can consequently include a fixed host whose schedule excludes that day. Reject slots unless a working-hours interval on the slot's weekday contains the event, when no date override applies.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Timezone conversion takes only hour and minute, discarding day rollover and turning intervals crossing attendee midnight into reversed ranges. A UTC organizer's 22:00–23:00 override viewed in UTC+01:30 becomes startTime 1410 and endTime 30, which buildSlots skips because start is greater than end, removing valid availability. Preserve the converted dates and split the interval across attendee-day boundaries before building slots.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Do not return true before checking busy intervals when a date override matches. For example, with a 09:00–17:00 override and an existing 10:00–11:00 booking, a candidate at 10:00 sets dateOverrideExist and returns true here, bypassing busy.every entirely. The fixed-host filtering and loose-host assignment both call this predicate with date overrides, so an already-booked host can be advertised as available. Let a valid override bypass only the normal working-hours check, then continue through the busy checks.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Do not return true before checking busy periods when a date override exists. Previously, checkIfIsAvailable rejected overlapping calendar events/bookings (apart from the explicit currentSeats exception), and the fixed-host and loose-host consumers still rely on that behavior when passing their schedules. With this early return, any slot accepted by the override branch is considered available even if the host has a conflicting booking. Let the override bypass only the normal working-hours check, then continue through busy.every.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: A matching date override returns true before the busy.every check below. Consequently a host with an override is considered available even when an existing booking or calendar busy interval overlaps the slot. An override should replace normal working hours, not bypass busy-time checks; continue to the busy check after validating the override.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The variable named end is calculated from slotStartTime, exactly like start, instead of slotEndTime. A slot starting at 16:45 with a 30-minute duration passes a working-hours window ending at 17:00 despite ending at 17:15. Calculate the end boundary from the slot end.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: This search rejects a slot if it falls outside any working-hours window on that weekday. With split hours of 09:00–12:00 and 13:00–17:00, a valid 10:00 slot is rejected because it is outside the afternoon window. Check for containment in at least one applicable window rather than finding any window that excludes the slot.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The equality check compares two separately created Dayjs objects with ===, which is always false, even when the override start and end represent the same instant. The intended zero-length/closed-day rejection is unreachable, and a slot beginning exactly at that instant can reach the dateOverrideExist success return. Compare timestamps or use isSame instead.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The async forEach callback moves calendar factory exceptions outside the surrounding try/catch because forEach discards its returned promise. An invalid encrypted Exchange credential throws during CalendarService construction, now producing an unhandled rejection while Reschedule continues and returns success instead of logging the error; the identical regression occurs in wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts. Await Promise.all over bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...) inside the try block, or use an awaited for...of loop, so factory and deletion failures reach the catch.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The new async forEach callback is not awaited. If getCalendar rejects (for example, the dynamically imported calendar module fails to load or its service constructor throws), the callback produces a rejected promise that forEach discards; the surrounding try/catch cannot catch it. Previously a synchronous getCalendar failure reached that catch. Await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...)) or use an awaited for...of loop so these failures remain handled and calendar cleanup completes before rescheduling continues. Apply the same fix to the equivalent changed loop in wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Deferred cancellation includes reminders less than ten minutes from their scheduled send time, when SendGrid no longer permits cancellation. A booking cancelled in that interval is only marked cancelled locally by deleteScheduledEmailReminder, and the cron's POST is rejected, so its email is still delivered. Process cancellation before SendGrid's ten-minute cutoff and explicitly handle cancellations that arrive after that deadline rather than relying on this cron query to stop delivery.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Successful cancellation records are only deleted after every SendGrid request in the loop succeeds. If a later request fails, the catch skips all queued Prisma deletions; the next run retries an already-cancelled batch, which SendGrid rejects with 400, and aborts before processing the remaining reminders. Await each reminder's database deletion immediately after its successful cancellation and isolate errors per reminder so one failed batch does not block the others.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Cancellation now delegates the database update/deletion to asynchronous reminder helpers without awaiting them, while removing reminder deletes from the awaited promise list. The handler can finish before cancelled flags or unscheduled-reminder deletions are persisted, allowing a subsequent scheduler run to schedule a cancelled booking's reminder and leaving cancellation work unfinished when a serverless invocation terminates. Collect and await the helper promises; apply the same correction to the modified rescheduling and workflow-update callers that discard these promises.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Await the reminder cancellation promises before completing the cancellation request. These helpers now own persistence of cancellation: email awaits a workflowReminder update and SMS awaits Twilio before deleting the row. The forEach discards their promises, and removing remindersToDelete from the awaited promise list removes the previous guarantee that reminder state is cleared before the handler returns. In a serverless request the outstanding operations can be interrupted after the response, leaving reminders active for a cancelled booking. Collect these helper promises and include them in the awaited Promise.all.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Await the reminder cancellation helpers as part of the handler's Promise.all. Previously this handler awaited deletion of every workflowReminder through remindersToDelete; now the only database deletion/marking occurs inside these async helpers, but their promises are discarded by forEach. The request can complete before email reminders are marked cancelled (or SMS/unscheduled reminders are deleted), and a serverless invocation can stop before that cleanup completes, leaving reminders active for a cancelled booking. Collect the helper promises and include them in the awaited work instead of removing the awaited cleanup altogether.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Handle cancellation failures per reminder rather than around the entire batch. If one SendGrid request rejects (for example, for an expired or invalid batch ID), the loop exits before cancelling the remaining reminders, and Promise.all is never reached, so even earlier successfully cancelled reminders remain in the database. The failed record stays eligible for the next run and can repeatedly block other cancellations until their emails are sent. Execute each successful deletion and isolate failures so the worker continues processing the remaining reminders.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Await the reminder-manager calls as part of the cancellation work (for example, collect their promises and include them in Promise.all). Both changed helpers now perform the database cleanup themselves: email reminders are marked cancelled and SMS/unscheduled reminders are deleted asynchronously. This loop discards those promises, and the previously awaited reminder deletion promises have been removed. The handler can therefore finish before cancellation is persisted; in a serverless deployment that suspends execution after the response, cancelled bookings can retain active reminders. Apply the same awaited-call contract to the other callers that removed their awaited database cleanup.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Successful cache deletion does not invalidate the connectedCalendars query that supplies cacheUpdatedAt. The wrapper forwards only an optional parent onChanged callback and disables window-focus refetch, so the deleted cache continues to appear present with its old timestamp and delete action. Invalidate utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars on successful deletion.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The new timestamp update passes an empty data object to Prisma updateMany, which does not advance @updatedAt. SelectedCalendar.updatedAt therefore remains unchanged after cache repopulation instead of recording the refresh as this new side effect intends. Pass { updatedAt: new Date() } explicitly.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The environment update uses BSD sed's `-i ''` syntax, which fails with GNU sed on Linux. When GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL already exists, the script leaves the previous URL unchanged but still prints that it was updated, preventing webhooks from reaching the new tunnel. Use a portable replacement strategy or select the in-place syntax based on the available sed implementation and check its exit status.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The empty update object does not update Prisma's @updatedAt field (empty updates leave it unchanged), so this call does not perform the timestamp refresh described by the comment. Pass an explicit updatedAt value if successful cache refreshes are intended to advance SelectedCalendar.updatedAt.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: When GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL already exists, `sed -i ''` uses BSD/macOS syntax and fails under GNU sed on Linux. The script nevertheless prints that the URL was updated and keeps the tunnel running, leaving webhooks configured with the old URL. Use a portable replacement approach (or select the appropriate sed syntax) and only announce success after the edit succeeds.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The new call does not actually refresh SelectedCalendar.updatedAt. updateManyByCredentialId in the other changed file forwards `data` unchanged to Prisma, and Prisma does not advance an @updatedAt field when the update data is empty. Consequently successful availability refreshes leave the selected-calendar timestamps unchanged despite this call's stated purpose. Pass an explicit timestamp, e.g. `{ updatedAt: new Date() }`, or make the repository method explicitly perform the timestamp update.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The cache timestamp is always formatted with "en-US", even though the surrounding label uses the user's selected translation locale. Users in other locales therefore see US month/day ordering and time conventions inside an otherwise localized message, potentially misreading the last-update date. Use the active application locale for Intl.DateTimeFormat instead of hard-coding en-US.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: This warning says updatedAt is added without a default and cannot be added to a nonempty table, but the migration actually supplies DEFAULT NOW(), explicitly handling existing rows. Remove or correct the warning so operators reviewing the migration are not incorrectly told that existing data makes it unsafe to run.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Updating match statistics inside email validation counts a single blocked signup twice. UsersController#create calls user.valid? and then user.save, which validates again even when the first validation failed, so both invocations increment match_count. Record the attempt once at the signup boundary rather than as a side effect of each validation.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The match_count update is a read-modify-write operation without synchronization. Concurrent signup attempts for the same blocked email can both read the same count and save the same incremented value, losing matches and potentially overwriting last_match_at with an older timestamp. Use an atomic database increment with the timestamp update, or lock the row before reading and updating its statistics.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: Blocked-email lookup compares the raw email without normalizing its domain. A signup for block@SPAMFROMHOME.ORG does not match a blocked record for block@spamfromhome.org despite identifying the same mailbox, allowing the signup restriction to be bypassed by changing domain capitalization. Normalize domains using Email.downcase both when storing blocked emails and when looking them up.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: Canonicalize blocked emails consistently with the application's Email.downcase identity handling, both when storing entries and when looking them up. This exact equality query is case-sensitive, and BlockedEmail's validation callback only defaults action_type. A block-list entry such as `Block@SpamFromHome.org` therefore does not block the same identity submitted/stored as `block@spamfromhome.org`. This is particularly relevant to the explicitly supported manually populated block list. Normalize existing/imported entries as well as new ones, and add a test with differing casing between the stored entry and the lookup.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The match counter update loses increments under concurrent validations. If two requests load a blocked email with match_count N before either saves, both assign N+1 and save, leaving N+1 despite two matches (and a later save can also overwrite a newer last_match_at). Use an atomic database increment with the timestamp update, or lock and reload the row before modifying the statistics.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The match counter loses increments under concurrent validations. Two calls can both load match_count = N, increment their separate records to N + 1, and save that same value, recording only one of two matches. Use an atomic database increment (or serialize the read/update with a row lock) so match_count measures every matching validation rather than only non-overlapping ones.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The unsubscribe action dereferences the result of TopicUser.find_by without handling a missing record. A logged-in user visiting the unsubscribe URL for a visible topic they have not previously visited gets a NoMethodError instead of being unsubscribed, because TopicView does not create that row. Handle the absent row with the regular default notification level and persist the selection through TopicUser.change, which supports creating missing records.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Saving the notification level directly leaves notifications_reason_id unchanged instead of recording an explicit user choice. For automatically tracked topics with a null reason, TopicUser.update_last_read promotes the row back to tracking when the reading threshold is exceeded, undoing the unsubscribe on the next read. Persist the change through TopicUser.change so notifications_reason_id and notifications_changed_at are set consistently with set_notifications.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The client unsubscribe route only loads the ordinary topic view and never performs the unsubscribe operation. When entered through an in-app transition rather than a full server navigation, PostStream.loadTopicView requests /t/:id.json (or consumes preload data), so the page claims notifications will stop while the persisted notification level remains unchanged. Ensure this entry path executes the unsubscribe operation before showing confirmation.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: The new GET routes mutate the authenticated user's notification preferences without CSRF verification. An attacker can navigate a logged-in user's browser to a known topic unsubscribe URL and reduce or mute its notifications, because Rails excludes GET from forgery-token checks and unsubscribe explicitly skips check_xhr. Make GET render a confirmation page and perform the preference change through a CSRF-protected POST or PUT.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The confirmation promises that the user will stop receiving notifications for this topic, but TopicsController#unsubscribe sets watching/tracking users to regular, not muted. Regular still allows mention/reply notifications, so this confirmation (and the corresponding promise in the new email link text) overstates what clicking the link accomplished. Describe stopping notifications for every new post, or make the confirmation conditional on the resulting notification level so only muted users are told that all topic notifications have stopped.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Make the unsubscribe URL absolute before passing it to the email builder (for example, prepend Discourse.base_url). Topic#unsubscribe_url appends `/unsubscribe` to the topic's site-relative URL, but the new server translation interpolates unsubscribe_url directly into an email Markdown link and MessageBuilder cooks it without adding the site origin. Unlike the post link in notification.html.erb, which explicitly prepends Discourse.base_url, this produces a `/t/.../unsubscribe` href that email clients cannot resolve to the forum, so the new per-topic unsubscribe link does not work reliably.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Handle a missing TopicUser record before dereferencing it. A logged-in user can visit this URL for a topic they have not tracked or visited (for example, an unsubscribe link forwarded by another user); find_by then returns nil and tu.notification_level raises NoMethodError, returning a 500 instead of unsubscribing. Find or initialize the user's topic record, applying the default notification level before updating it.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The client route loads the topic but never invokes the unsubscribe action. Notification levels are changed only by TopicsController#unsubscribe, so navigating to this route inside the Ember application can display “You will stop receiving notifications” without changing the subscription. Explicitly perform the unsubscribe operation on client-side entry rather than relying on the initial HTML request to have done it.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Saving the notification level directly bypasses the explicit-user-change metadata set by TopicUser.change. In particular, a topic_user with notifications_reason_id == nil remains eligible for TopicUser.auto_track, which checks that field and can promote the topic back to tracking after the user unsubscribes. Use the notification-change helper (or set its user-change reason and timestamp consistently) so the unsubscribe is retained as an explicit user preference.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The dark-theme notification badge background now uses a lightened $secondary while its text still uses the unmodified $secondary. This puts dark text on a dark background for plain badges such as category unread counts in site-map.hbs:73; with $secondary black, the foreground is #000 and the background is approximately #4d4d4d (about 2.5:1 contrast), making the small count text difficult to read. Set the default badge foreground, including its &[href] rule, to a contrasting dark-theme color such as $primary when selecting this dark background.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Preserve the original 30% primary lightness in the light-theme argument (and use 70% secondary lightness for its dark equivalent). This replacement changes 30% to 70%, so the bold reply author link becomes substantially paler even in the existing light theme, rather than merely adding dark-theme support.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The custom-message-length light/dark percentages are reversed relative to both the original rule and the desktop rule at desktop/modal.scss:94. Use primary 70% and secondary 30% here. As written, mobile displays a much stronger message-length hint than desktop in both themes, and changes the existing light-theme output.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Keep primary lightness at 20% for the light-theme branch and use secondary 80% for the dark branch, matching desktop/topic-post.scss:321. The new 50%/50% pair unnecessarily fades the mobile h3 text in light themes and makes the same heading less prominent on mobile than desktop in dark themes.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Hostname comparisons are case-sensitive even though DNS hostnames are case-insensitive. With an instance hostname of example.com and a valid website of http://EXAMPLE.COM/user, neither the exact-host nor suffix comparison matches, so the profile displays only EXAMPLE.COM instead of the requested path. Normalize both hostnames to lowercase for comparison while preserving the desired display spelling.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Comparing all labels except the first incorrectly treats unrelated domains under multi-label public suffixes as the same domain. For example, with instance host `forum.co.uk` and website `https://unrelated.co.uk/user`, this returns `unrelated.co.uk/user` rather than the unrelated-site host-only label. Both hosts have three labels and their suffixes are `co.uk`, so this branch mistakes the public suffix for a shared site domain. Use registrable-domain-aware comparison (or a narrower explicit host relationship) before including the path.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: Apply the same untrusted-attribute visibility policy to website_name as to website. website is listed in untrusted_attributes, which hides it for TL0 users viewed anonymously, but include_website_name checks only website.present?. Anonymous responses can therefore disclose the hidden website's hostname (and its path for matching domains) through this new field even when website itself is omitted.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The newly interpolated targets are interpolated again by DataSourceWithBackend.query when runQuery executes each split request. TemplateSrv.replace scans the resulting string again, so a variable whose literal value contains another defined variable token (for example, a log-search value containing `$other`) is expanded a second time and produces a different query from the non-splitting path; shard splitting also passes through this additional interpolation. Preserve the early interpolation needed for partitioning while ensuring already-interpolated targets are not interpolated again on execution, and test through the real backend query preparation rather than mocking runQuery.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The replacement DB does not preserve the behavior required by its consumers: RunCommands and QueryFramesInto now always return "not implemented". sql.TablesList still calls RunCommands to discover dependencies, and SQL command construction calls that parser, so even valid SQL can no longer construct a command; commands reaching Execute also cannot produce frames. Implement the backing operations (or retain the existing duck implementation) before switching these consumers to this DB.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: enableSqlExpressions returns false on both paths, including when FlagSqlExpressions is enabled. Consequently ReadQuery rejects every SQL expression and the enabled feature branch can never execute. Return the actual feature-enabled state rather than unconditionally returning false.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The replacement database unconditionally returns "not implemented" from both RunCommands and QueryFramesInto. parser.TablesList now uses the former and SQLCommand.Execute uses the latter, so previously supported SQL parsing and execution always fail, even if the feature gate is corrected. Preserve the working database implementation or provide equivalent operations before switching these callers.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The denial cache key does not distinguish underscores inside resource and parent UIDs from its field separators. For the same namespace, user and action, (name="a_b", parent="c") and (name="a", parent="b_c") generate the same key, so denying the first request makes Check return false for the second even if its permissions explicitly allow it. Encode the components unambiguously, for example as a JSON tuple or length-prefixed fields.

suggestions.label: performance
suggestions.suggestionContent: Every distinct resource denied by the cached permission map triggers a reload of the entire user's action permission set, because the denial cache is resource-specific and a cached false result always falls through to getIdentityPermissions. Sequential checks of N inaccessible dashboards therefore execute N full permission queries and cache rewrites even with a current action-wide cache; getUserPermissions' singleflight only merges overlapping requests. Bound refreshes per user/action with a short refresh cooldown or generation marker so different resource misses can share a recent refresh.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The denial cache key is not injective: for the same namespace, user and action, `(name="a_b", parent="c")` and `(name="a", parent="b_c")` produce the same key. After the first request stores a denial, Check's new early cache return denies the second request without checking its permissions, even if it is allowed. Encode the components unambiguously (for example a JSON tuple or length-prefixed components) and add a test verifying that these two requests do not share a denial entry.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The comment says this seeds an allow permission to prove that the denial cache takes precedence, but the seeded permission is false. This contradicts the documented test setup and does not establish the claimed allow-versus-deny scenario. Seed the dashboard permission with true so the fixture matches the comment and demonstrates the intended precedence.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Make the denial-cache key encode component boundaries unambiguously (for example, length-prefix or serialize the components). For the same namespace, user and action, name `a_b` with parent `c` and name `a` with parent `b_c` both produce the suffix `_a_b_c`. Underscores can occur in resource UIDs, so denying the first request caches a key that causes Check to immediately deny the second request without evaluating its permissions, even if that resource is allowed.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Encode the denial-key components unambiguously rather than joining them with underscores. For the same namespace, user and action, (name="a_b", parent="c") and (name="a", parent="b_c") produce the same key. Check in service.go now treats any hit on this key as an unconditional denial before checking permissions, so a denial for one dashboard/folder pair can deny a different, authorized pair until expiry. Use a structured or length-prefixed encoding (or escaping) that preserves component boundaries, and add a test covering these two distinct tuples.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The fixture described as allowing access sets `"dashboards:uid:dash1"` to `false`. This does not establish the competing allow that the explicit-denial-cache test is supposed to override, so a denial alone cannot prove that the denial-cache lookup worked. Set the permission to `true`, and verify that the same request is allowed without the denial entry before asserting that the entry makes it denied. This makes the test fail if denial-cache precedence is removed.

suggestions.label: performance
suggestions.suggestionContent: The SQLite literal-ID path rebuilds the entire accumulated string for every ID, making SQL construction quadratic in batch size. Large batches explicitly supported by this PR, including the 32,767 setting in the integration test, generate substantial repeated copying and allocation before each delete, consuming cleanup time and memory. Build the list with strings.Builder and append each formatted ID once.

suggestions.label: performance
suggestions.suggestionContent: The ticker change runs the entire cleanup service every minute instead of every ten minutes, not just annotation cleanup. The clean method also processes temporary files, snapshots, dashboard versions, images, invites, short URLs and query history, increasing their database and filesystem workload tenfold; cycles lasting over a minute also leave a pending tick that starts another cycle immediately afterward. Preserve the ten-minute interval for the shared cleanup service, or schedule annotations independently if they require a shorter interval.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The comment states that SQLite has a parameter limit of 999, but SQLite >= 3.32.0 defaults to 32766 (as the added integration test also recognizes). This branch is choosing a conservative compatibility threshold, not expressing the limit of every SQLite database. Document 999 as the older-version/compatibility threshold so maintainers do not mistake this constant for the actual limit on modern SQLite.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The new SQLite-limit regression case does not exceed the parameter limit when deleting annotations. The 40,003 fixtures are distributed across alert, dashboard and API types, and CleanAnnotations selects/deletes each type separately, so each annotation DELETE receives only about 13,333 IDs despite the configured batch size of 32,767. On SQLite >=3.32.0, switching annotation deletion back to placeholders would therefore still pass this test (the tag cleanup can independently retain its workaround). Create more than 32,767 annotations of a single type, or enough total fixtures for at least one type's deletion to exceed 32,766 parameters, and assert that cleanup succeeds.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: readSequence accepts a child whose encoded size exceeds the remaining declared sequence length. For example, `30 04 02 01 01 02 01 01` is accepted as a two-integer sequence even though its children occupy six bytes rather than the declared four, so asn1derToConcatenatedRS silently converts malformed DER instead of rejecting it. Restrict child decoding to the sequence's declared content boundary and throw IOException when a child exceeds the remaining length.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The newly registered client CryptoProvider does not satisfy the existing EC JWK parsing consumer: core's AbstractJWKParser calls createECParams(name) and getKeyFactory("ECDSA") to construct an EC public key, and both operations now throw UnsupportedOperationException when this provider is selected. Consequently, a standalone authz client using this provider cannot parse EC keys for ECDSA verification, even though signature conversion is implemented. Implement the JDK-backed curve-parameter and key-factory operations (mapping ECDSA to EC as needed), rather than leaving this existing consumer with an unsupported contract.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Bound each child TLV to the remaining sequence length before accepting it. Currently readNext() reads from the whole input and length may become negative, which silently ends the loop successfully. For example, `30 05 02 01 01 02 01 01` is accepted as a two-integer sequence although the second INTEGER crosses the declared sequence boundary. Decode through a stream limited to the sequence content, or reject a child whose encoded size exceeds the remaining length, so malformed DER cannot be converted as a valid signature.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: Reject ambiguous highest-priority providers rather than silently taking the first. Both DefaultCryptoProvider and FIPS1402Provider return order 200 in this PR, so when both are present the stable sort leaves the decision to ServiceLoader discovery order. A deployment expecting FIPS can therefore initialize the ordinary Bouncy Castle provider without an error; previously this mixed classpath failed closed. Preserve the error for tied highest-priority providers (or require an explicit security-mode/provider choice), while still allowing the lower-priority authz-client fallback.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The assertion only establishes agreement between the two new conversion routines, not correctness of the converted signature. For example, swapping r and s in both routines makes this entire round trip pass, although the DER result no longer verifies the signed data. Verify `asn1Des` with the public key and original data (or compare against an independently specified encoding) so mutually compensating conversion defects fail the test.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Every case generates a default EC key rather than a key on the curve associated with the named algorithm. On the standard JDK this is P-256, so testES384 and testES512 just pad P-256 signature components to larger lengths. A converter that discards nonzero high bytes beyond 32 bytes would still pass all three cases. Initialize the key generator with the appropriate curve per case (P-256, P-384, and P-521) so the larger-component conversions are actually tested.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Reject a child whose encoded length exceeds the remaining sequence length. Currently bytes `30 01 02 01 01` declare a one-byte sequence body but readSequence returns the entire three-byte INTEGER and exits with length -2. Consequently malformed sequence boundaries are treated as successfully decoded results. Bound child reads to the sequence body and require the remainder to reach exactly zero.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Generate a key on the curve corresponding to each tested algorithm rather than using the provider's default EC curve for all three tests. On the standard JDK this generates a P-256 key even for testES384 and testES512, so those tests merely pad P-256 integers to larger output lengths and never exercise actual P-384/P-521 signature encoding (including P-521's long-form sequence length).

suggestions.label: performance
suggestions.suggestionContent: Remove these two discarded encoder writes. Each allocates an encoder and encodes a BigInteger, but neither result participates in the returned signature; lines 119–120 repeat both writes on fresh encoders. This performs redundant encoding and allocations on every concatenated-signature conversion.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Enforce the declared SEQUENCE boundary before reading each child and reject children whose full encoding exceeds the remaining length. For example, `30 04 02 01 01 02 01 02` declares only four content bytes, but this loop reads both three-byte INTEGER encodings, lets length become -2, and returns a two-element sequence. Consequently asn1derToConcatenatedRS accepts a malformed DER signature by consuming bytes outside its enclosing sequence. Parse through a bounded content stream and require exact consumption.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Reject INTEGER values that do not fit the requested component width instead of silently dropping their high bytes. Removing a single leading sign-padding zero is valid, but this branch also truncates actual magnitude bytes: a positive value 2^256 + 1 becomes 1 when qLength is 32. Thus DER-to-concatenated conversion can return a different signature from the one supplied. Validate nonnegative values and their bit length before padding or removing sign padding.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: canManage() grants management access for an all-groups VIEW permission. Inherited requireManage() uses this result in GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup, allowing a view-only administrator to create groups or reparent an existing group to the top level. Evaluate only AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE here.

suggestions.label: bug
